questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A trade association in State A was formed for the purpose of protecting the state's lucrative cattle industry. The association's members, who are cattle breeders and dealers, use a grading system to grade the quality of cattle bred in the state. The grades assigned by the association are nationally recognized and prominently displayed on cattle to promote the state's cattle industry.
The commissioner of the agency that regulates cattle in State B has adopted a regulation that requires cattle sold in the state to display a grade approved by the federal government or no grade at all. The sales in State B of several members of the trade association have declined as a result of complying with this regulation. As a result, the association has filed suit against the commissioner in a federal district court, seeking an injunction against the enforcement of the regulation on the ground that it is unconstitutional.
May the court determine the merits of this suit?

choices.A: No, because the association itself has suffered no injury.
choices.B: No, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits suits against state officials in federal court.
choices.C: Yes, because federal courts have exclusive jurisdiction over federal-law claims.
choices.D: Yes, because the association has standing to sue on behalf of its members.

questions.explanation:
Article III standing
(suing on another's behalf)
Organization members Organization has standing if:
  • members have standing to sue on their own behalf
  • their injuries relate to organization's purpose AND
  • lawsuit does not require member participation (if damages sought)
Third party Injured plaintiff has standing when:
  • important relationship between litigant & third party (e.g., physician-patient)
  • lack of ability of third party to vindicate own rights OR
  • risk that third party's rights will be diluted if third-party standing is not allowed
Child Parent has standing unless parental rights have been limited by court OR lawsuit may adversely affect child
Assignor Assignee has standing if assigned legal claim for ordinary & good-faith business purpose

A federal court cannot hear a case unless the plaintiff has standing—ie, a concrete interest in the outcome of the case—to bring it. When the plaintiff is an organization (eg, trade association), the organization has standing to sue when it has suffered an injury. It also has standing to bring an action on behalf of its members when:

  • the members themselves would have standing to sue (ie, members suffered an injury-in-fact that was caused by the defendant and is redressable by the remedy sought)
  • the interests at stake (eg, members' injuries) relate to the organization's purpose and
  • if damages are sought, the lawsuit does not require member participation (eg, to prove monetary damages).

Here, the association's members would have standing because the decline in sales (injury-in-fact) caused by the commissioner's regulation (causation) will be remedied if the court grants an injunction (redressability). The decline in sales relates to the association's purpose of protecting State A's cattle industry. And since the association seeks an injunction (not damages), member participation is not needed. Therefore, the association has standing to sue on behalf of its members, and the court may determine the merits of this suit.

(Choice A) An organization must suffer an injury-in-fact to have standing to sue on its own behalf. But an organization may have standing to sue on its members' behalf even if it has not suffered an injury.

(Choice B) The Eleventh Amendment generally bars private parties and foreign governments from suing a state in federal court for monetary relief. But it does not bar suits against state officials for injunctive relief (as seen here).

(Choice C) Federal and state courts have concurrent jurisdiction over federal-law claims unless the Constitution or Congress expressly provides federal courts with exclusive jurisdiction (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

An organization has standing to sue on its members' behalf when (1) the members themselves would have standing to sue, (2) the interests at stake relate to the organization's purpose, and (3) if damages are sought, the lawsuit does not require member participation.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case-or-controversy requirement).
  • Hunt v. Wash. State Apple Adver. Comm'n, 432 U.S. 333, 343–45 (1977) (holding that organizations may bring actions on behalf of their members when the requirements for organizational standing are met.)
questions.zh-question:
某A州的一个行业协会成立，旨在保护该州利润丰厚的养牛业。该协会的成员是养牛者和经销商，他们使用一套分级系统来评估该州所养牛的品质。协会评定的等级在全国范围内得到认可，并醒目地展示在牛身上，以推广该州的养牛业。
B州负责监管牛的机构的专员通过了一项法规，要求在该州出售的牛必须展示联邦政府批准的等级，或者根本不展示任何等级。由于遵守这项法规，该行业协会的几位成员在B州的销售额有所下降。因此，该协会已在联邦地区法院对该专员提起诉讼，寻求一项针对该法规执行的禁令（injunction），理由是该法规违宪。
法院能否审理此案的实体问题（merits）？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为协会本身并未遭受损害（injury）。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为第十一修正案（Eleventh Amendment）禁止在联邦法院起诉州官员。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为联邦法院对联邦法律主张（federal-law claims）拥有专属管辖权（exclusive jurisdiction）。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为协会有代表其成员提起诉讼的诉讼资格（standing）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法：司法审查

正确答案：D

判决要点：一个协会可以代表其成员提起诉讼，前提是其成员本身具有诉讼资格，诉讼涉及的利益与协会的宗旨相关，并且诉讼（尤其是寻求禁令救济时）不需要成员的个体参与。

核心法律规则：协会代表其成员提起诉讼的资格 (Organizational Standing)

协会代表其成员提起诉讼的资格

根据美国宪法第三条，联邦法院只能审理“案件或争议” (cases or controversies)。原告必须具有诉讼资格 (standing)，即对案件结果有具体的利害关系。当原告是一个组织（例如行业协会）时，该组织可以代表其成员提起诉讼，如果满足以下三个条件：

  • 其成员本身具有诉讼资格 (have standing to sue)，即成员遭受了事实上的损害 (injury-in-fact)，且该损害是由被告造成的，并且可以通过法院寻求的救济来补救 (redressability)。
  • 诉讼涉及的利益 (interests at stake) 与组织的宗旨 (organization's purpose) 相关联。
  • 如果寻求的是损害赔偿 (damages)，则诉讼通常需要成员的个体参与；但如果寻求的是禁令救济 (injunctive relief)，则诉讼通常不需要成员的个体参与。

概念比较：代表他人提起诉讼的资格 (Standing on Another's Behalf)

类型 具有诉讼资格的条件
组织成员 (Organization Members) 成员本身具有诉讼资格；其损害与组织宗旨相关联；诉讼不要求成员个体参与（如果寻求损害赔偿）。
第三方 (Third Party) 受伤的原告具有诉讼资格，且与第三方有重要关系（例如，医生-病人）；第三方缺乏能力维护自身权利；或者如果不允许第三方诉讼，第三方的权利将被稀释。
子女 (Child) 父母具有诉讼资格，除非父母的权利主张会对其子女造成不利影响。
受让人 (Assignor) 受让人 (assignee) 具有诉讼资格，如果其法律主张是出于普通且善意的商业目的而转让的。

事实分析与法律适用

本案中，州A的贸易协会的成员因遵守州B的规定而导致销售额下降，这构成了事实上的损害 (injury-in-fact)。如果法院批准禁令，该损害可以得到补救 (redressability)。因此，成员本身具有诉讼资格。

该协会的宗旨是保护州A利润丰厚的畜牧业。州B的规定影响了成员的牲畜销售，这与协会的宗旨直接相关。

由于协会寻求的是禁令救济 (injunction)，而非损害赔偿 (damages)，因此诉讼不需要成员的个体参与来证明损害或计算赔偿。所有条件均已满足。

因此，法院可以审理此案的实体问题。

协会诉讼资格流程图

协会提起诉讼

↓

成员是否具有诉讼资格？
(Injury-in-fact & Redressability)

↓

利益是否与协会宗旨相关？

↓

是否需要成员个体参与？
(寻求禁令通常不需要)

↓

所有条件满足 → 协会具有诉讼资格

考点陷阱与易混淆概念

陷阱一：误认为组织必须遭受直接损害。 许多考生错误地认为，只有当组织本身遭受了直接损害时，它才能提起诉讼。但实际上，组织可以代表其成员提起诉讼，即使组织本身没有直接损害，只要其成员满足诉讼资格的要求，并且其他组织诉讼资格的条件也得到满足。

陷阱二：混淆禁令救济与损害赔偿对成员参与的要求。 记住，如果寻求的是禁令救济，通常不需要成员的个体参与；但如果寻求的是损害赔偿，则通常需要成员的个体参与来证明损害和计算赔偿金额。

正确答案与干扰项排除

D. 是，因为该协会有资格代表其成员提起诉讼。

正确。根据组织诉讼资格的规则，本案中的协会满足所有条件：成员遭受了销售额下降的事实损害，且该损害可通过禁令救济；诉讼涉及的利益（保护畜牧业）与协会宗旨相关；且由于寻求的是禁令，不需要成员的个体参与。因此，协会具有代表其成员提起诉讼的资格。

A. 否，因为协会本身没有遭受任何损害。

错误。虽然协会本身可能没有遭受直接损害，但它可以代表其成员提起诉讼，只要其成员满足诉讼资格的要求，并且其他组织诉讼资格的条件也得到满足。本案中，成员遭受了损害，因此协会可以代表他们提起诉讼。

B. 否，因为第十一修正案禁止在联邦法院起诉州官员。

错误。第十一修正案 (Eleventh Amendment) 通常禁止私人当事人起诉州政府或州机构。然而，它不禁止私人当事人在联邦法院起诉州官员以寻求禁令救济 (injunctive relief)，以阻止其违反联邦法律的行为。本案中，协会正是寻求对州官员的禁令救济。

C. 是，因为联邦法院对联邦法律主张拥有专属管辖权。

错误。联邦法院对联邦法律主张并不总是拥有专属管辖权 (exclusive jurisdiction)。在许多情况下，州法院和联邦法院对联邦法律主张拥有并行管辖权 (concurrent jurisdiction)。只有当国会明确规定或宪法明确要求时，联邦法院才拥有专属管辖权。

备考小贴士

在判断组织诉讼资格时，务必牢记三个核心要素：成员自身有诉讼资格、利益与组织宗旨相关、以及是否需要成员个体参与（禁令救济通常不需要）。这是MBE常考的知识点。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress provides funds to states that can be used to reimburse medical providers for procedures they perform for low-income individuals. A state that participates in this federal program enacted a statute that prohibits reimbursing providers for the cost of performing vasectomies for men.
A doctor who routinely performs vasectomies for low-income men has submitted numerous requests for reimbursement pursuant to the program. However, the commissioner of the state agency administering the program has repeatedly denied the doctor's requests pursuant to the state statute.
The doctor sued the commissioner in a federal district court, seeking an injunction against the enforcement of the statute on the ground that it violates men's right to privacy.
Assuming that this federal district court has previously held that men have a privacy right to obtain vasectomies, how should the district court proceed with the doctor's suit?

choices.A: Determine the merits of the suit, because federal courts have exclusive jurisdiction over federal-law claims.
choices.B: Determine the merits of the suit, because the doctor has standing.
choices.C: Refuse to adjudicate the merits of the suit and dismiss it, because the Eleventh Amendment bars this type of action in federal court.
choices.D: Refuse to adjudicate the merits of the suit and stay the suit until a man seeking a vasectomy joins the suit.

questions.explanation:
Article III standing
(suing on another's behalf)
Organization members
Organization has standing if:
  • members have standing to sue on their own behalf
  • their injuries relate to organization's purpose AND
  • lawsuit does not require member participation (if damages sought)
Third party
Injured plaintiff has standing when:
  • important relationship between litigant & third party (e.g., physician-patient)
  • lack of ability of third party to vindicate own rights OR
  • risk that third party's rights will be diluted if third-party standing is not allowed
Child Parent has standing unless parental rights have been limited by court OR lawsuit may adversely affect child
Assignor Assignee has standing if assigned legal claim for ordinary & good-faith business purpose

In federal litigation, parties are generally limited to asserting their own rights and not the rights of a third party. That is because the third party will likely be the most effective advocate of his/her own interests. However, the third-party standing doctrine permits an injured plaintiff to assert the rights of a third party when:

  • the plaintiff and the third party share an inextricably close relationship and
  • genuine obstacles prevent the third party from asserting his/her rights.

Here, enforcement of the statute harmed the doctor since he was denied reimbursement for performing vasectomies for men. Doctors share an inextricably close relationship with their patients. Additionally, the men's low-income status, fear of retaliation, and privacy concerns pose genuine obstacles that may prevent the men from challenging vasectomy restrictions. Therefore, the doctor has standing to assert that the statute violates men's right to privacy, and the court should hear the merits of the doctor's suit.

(Choice A) Federal and state courts have concurrent jurisdiction over federal-law claims unless the Constitution or Congress expressly provides federal courts with exclusive jurisdiction (not seen here).

(Choice C) The Eleventh Amendment generally bars federal courts from adjudicating suits against a state government for monetary relief—not suits against a state official for injunctive relief (as seen here).

(Choice D) A federal court can stay (ie, suspend) a suit to force a party to comply with a court order or protect a party's rights. But here, the federal court need not stay the action until a man seeking a vasectomy joins the suit because the doctor has third-party standing.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the third-party standing doctrine, an injured plaintiff may assert a third party's rights when (1) the parties share an inextricably close relationship and (2) genuine obstacles prevent the third party from asserting his/her rights.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case-or-controversy requirement).
  • Singleton v. Wulff, 428 U.S. 106, 118 (1976) (concluding that "it generally is appropriate to allow a physician to assert the rights of women patients as against governmental interference").
  • 16 Am. Jur. 2d Constitutional Law § 145 (2020) (explaining third-party standing requirements).
questions.zh-question:
国会向各州拨款，这些资金可用于报销医疗服务提供者为低收入个人实施医疗程序的费用。一个参与该联邦项目的州颁布了一项法规，禁止报销为男性进行输精管结扎术的费用。
一位经常为低收入男性进行输精管结扎术的医生，已根据该项目提交了多份报销请求。然而，负责管理该项目的州机构专员根据州法规，多次拒绝了该医生的请求。
该医生在联邦地区法院起诉了该专员，寻求禁止执行该法规的禁令，理由是该法规侵犯了男性的隐私权。
假设该联邦地区法院此前曾裁定男性拥有进行输精管结扎术的隐私权，地区法院应如何处理医生的诉讼？

zh-choices.A: 裁决诉讼的实体问题，因为联邦法院对联邦法律主张拥有专属管辖权。
zh-choices.B: 裁决诉讼的实体问题，因为该医生具有诉讼资格（standing）。
zh-choices.C: 拒绝裁决诉讼的实体问题并驳回诉讼，因为第十一修正案（Eleventh Amendment）禁止在联邦法院提起此类诉讼。
zh-choices.D: 拒绝裁决诉讼的实体问题并中止诉讼，直到一名寻求输精管结扎术的男性加入诉讼。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Judicial Review (宪法：司法审查)

正确答案：B
法院应审理案件的实体问题，因为医生具有第三方代位站立资格 (third-party standing)，可以主张其患者的权利。

核心法律原则：第三方代位站立 (Third-Party Standing)

第三方代位站立原则概述

在联邦诉讼中，当事人通常只能主张自己的权利，而不能主张第三方的权利。这是因为第三方通常是主张其自身利益最有效的倡导者。然而，第三方代位站立原则 (third-party standing doctrine) 允许受损害的原告主张第三方的权利，当满足以下两个条件时：

  • 原告与第三方之间存在不可分割的密切关系 (inextricably close relationship)。例如，医生与患者、律师与客户、销售商与买方等。
  • 存在真正的障碍 (genuine obstacles) 阻止第三方自行主张其权利。这些障碍可能包括：
    • 第三方缺乏能力主张自己的权利（如未成年人、心智障碍者）。
    • 如果不允许第三方代位站立，第三方的权利将面临被稀释或无法有效主张的风险。
    • 第三方因恐惧、经济困难、隐私担忧等原因不愿或无法提起诉讼。

不同类型的诉讼资格 (Standing) 比较

类型 站立条件 示例
组织成员 (Organization Members)
  • 成员有权以自己的名义起诉。
  • 成员的损害与组织的宗旨相关。
  • 诉讼不要求成员个人参与（如果寻求损害赔偿）。
 环保组织代表其成员起诉污染企业。
第三方 (Third Party)
  • 诉讼人与第三方之间存在重要关系（如医患关系）。
  • 第三方缺乏能力主张自己的权利，或。
  • 如果不允许第三方代位站立，第三方的权利将面临被稀释的风险。
 医生代表患者挑战堕胎限制。
子女 (Child)
  • 父母拥有诉讼资格，除非父母的权利主张会严重影响子女。
 父母代表子女起诉学校歧视。
受让人 (Assignor)
  • 受让人因正当、善意的商业目的被转让了合法索赔权，则具有诉讼资格。
 债权人将债务追索权转让给催收公司。

案情分析与法律适用

本案中，医生因州法规禁止报销男性输精管结扎手术费用而受到损害。医生向联邦地区法院提起诉讼，主张该法规侵犯了男性的隐私权。

  1. 原告受损害：医生因无法获得报销而遭受经济损失，满足了诉讼资格的“损害”要求。
  2. 不可分割的密切关系：医生与患者之间存在典型的不可分割的密切关系。医生在提供医疗服务时，直接受到影响患者权利的法规的制约。
  3. 真正的障碍：男性患者面临真正的障碍，阻止他们自行主张权利：
    • 低收入状况：患者可能因经济原因难以承担诉讼费用。
    • 对报复的恐惧：患者可能担心因挑战政府政策而遭受负面影响。
    • 隐私担忧：涉及生殖健康和医疗选择的问题高度个人化，患者可能不愿公开其医疗信息或参与诉讼。

鉴于医生与患者的密切关系以及患者面临的实际障碍，医生符合第三方代位站立的条件，可以代表男性患者主张其隐私权。因此，联邦地区法院应审理此案的实体问题。

概念图示：第三方代位站立

医生 (原告)
↓
不可分割的密切关系
↓
患者 (第三方)
↓
真正的障碍 (低收入、恐惧、隐私)
↓
医生代位主张患者权利

MBE 考点陷阱提示

在判断诉讼资格 (standing) 时，考生常犯的错误包括：

  • 混淆管辖权与诉讼资格：联邦法院对联邦法律主张通常拥有并行管辖权 (concurrent jurisdiction)，而非专属管辖权。因此，不能仅凭联邦法律主张就认为联邦法院拥有专属管辖权。
  • 误解第十一修正案：第十一修正案 (Eleventh Amendment) 主要禁止联邦法院审理针对州政府的货币赔偿诉讼。然而，针对州官员的禁令救济 (injunctive relief) 诉讼通常不受第十一修正案的限制。
  • 忽略第三方代位站立的例外：虽然一般原则是只能主张自己的权利，但当存在密切关系和真正的障碍时，第三方代位站立是允许的。不要轻易认为原告不能主张他人的权利而驳回案件。

正确答案与干扰项排除

B. 审理案件的实体问题，因为医生具有诉讼资格。

正确。根据第三方代位站立原则，医生与患者之间存在不可分割的密切关系，且患者因低收入、对报复的恐惧和隐私担忧而面临无法自行主张权利的真正障碍。因此，医生具有诉讼资格，法院应审理案件的实体问题。

A. 审理案件的实体问题，因为联邦法院对联邦法律主张拥有专属管辖权。

错误。联邦法院和州法院对联邦法律主张通常拥有并行管辖权 (concurrent jurisdiction)，除非宪法或国会明确规定联邦法院拥有专属管辖权 (exclusive jurisdiction)。本案中不存在专属管辖权的情况，因此该理由不成立。虽然法院确实应该审理实体问题，但原因不是专属管辖权。

C. 拒绝审理案件的实体问题并驳回诉讼，因为第十一修正案禁止联邦法院审理此类诉讼。

错误。第十一修正案 (Eleventh Amendment) 通常禁止联邦法院审理针对州政府的货币赔偿诉讼。然而，本案中医生寻求的是针对州机构专员的禁令救济 (injunctive relief)，而非货币赔偿。针对州官员的禁令救济诉讼通常不受第十一修正案的限制。

D. 拒绝审理案件的实体问题并中止诉讼，直到一名寻求输精管结扎手术的男性加入诉讼。

错误。法院可以中止诉讼以强制当事人遵守法院命令或保护当事人权利。但由于医生已具备第三方代位站立 (third-party standing) 资格，可以代表男性患者主张权利，因此法院无需中止诉讼等待患者加入。医生已经可以充分代表患者的利益。

MBE 备考小贴士

在判断诉讼资格 (standing) 时，请记住核心要素是：损害 (injury)、因果关系 (causation) 和可救济性 (redressability)。对于第三方代位站立 (third-party standing)，额外关注密切关系和真正的障碍。如果这些条件满足，法院应审理案件的实体问题，而不是以缺乏诉讼资格为由驳回。

参考文献

  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case-or-controversy requirement).
  • Singleton v. Wulff, 428 U.S. 106, 118 (1976) (concluding that "it generally is appropriate to allow a physician to assert the rights of women patients as against governmental interference").
  • 16 Am. Jur. 2d Constitutional Law § 145 (2020) (explaining third-party standing requirements).

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
An individual was physically removed from the premises of a privately owned shopping mall for passing out flyers in support of a candidate for mayor of the city in which the mall was located. The individual challenged this action in state court, contending that her removal violated the free speech provisions in both the U.S. and state constitutions. The trial court ruled in the individual's favor, and the mall properly appealed. The state supreme court concluded: "We hold that the state constitution, which protects free speech on privately owned property in certain situations, was clearly violated by the mall's conduct." The court declined to address the issue of whether that conduct violated the federal Constitution.
The United States Supreme Court granted a writ of certiorari to review this decision of the state supreme court.
How should the United States Supreme Court rule?

choices.A: Affirm the state supreme court's decision.
choices.B: Dismiss the writ as improvidently granted.
choices.C: Remand the case to the state supreme court.
choices.D: Reverse the state supreme court's decision.

questions.explanation:
SCOTUS review of state court decisions

(adequate & independent state grounds)
Was decision based on adequate
& independent state grounds?
Clearly yes
↓
No jurisdiction
Unclear
↓
Review federal issue
Clearly no
↓
Review federal issue
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States

The Supreme Court of the United States (SCOTUS) has discretion to review a final judgment issued by a state's highest court that turns on federal law. However, SCOTUS cannot review the merits of a state court judgment that rests on state-law grounds that are:

  • adequate – state law fully resolves the matter such that the application of federal law would not affect the outcome of the case and
  • independent – the state court clearly did not incorporate a federal standard by reference in reaching its conclusion.

And if a writ of certiorari was improvidently (i.e., incorrectly) granted in such a case, SCOTUS must dismiss the writ.

Here, the state supreme court's judgment was based on adequate state grounds because applying the federal Constitution would not affect the state court's finding that the mall violated the individual's free speech rights under the state constitution.* And the judgment was based on independent state grounds because the court declined to consider whether the federal Constitution was violated in ruling on the mall's appeal. Therefore, SCOTUS should dismiss the writ as improvidently granted.

*Remember that states are permitted to recognize individual rights that exceed those granted by the U.S. Constitution. Under the supremacy clause, federal law sets a floor below which state law cannot go, but it does not set a ceiling beyond which state law cannot go.

(Choices A and D) SCOTUS cannot review the merits of a state court judgment that rests on adequate and independent state grounds, so it cannot affirm or reverse the state supreme court's decision. Instead, it must decline to review the judgment entirely.

(Choice C) Remand to state court is permitted when it is unclear whether a state court's decision rests on state or federal law. In those circumstances, SCOTUS may hear the case, decide the federal issue, then remand the case to state court so that any question of state law can be resolved. But here, it is clear that the state court decision rests on adequate and independent state grounds.

📌 Educational Objective

SCOTUS has discretion to review a judgment issued by a state's highest court that turns on federal law, but it cannot review a state court judgment that rests on adequate and independent state-law grounds.

📚 References
  • Harris v. Reed, 489 U.S. 225, 260 (1989) (holding that the U.S. Supreme Court lacks jurisdiction to review a state court judgment that rests on an adequate and independent state-law ground).
questions.zh-question:
某个人因在一家私人拥有的购物中心内散发传单支持该市市长候选人而被强制驱离。该个人在州法院对这一行为提出质疑，声称她的驱离违反了美国宪法和州宪法中的言论自由条款。审理法院判决该个人胜诉，购物中心依法上诉。州最高法院裁定：“我们认为，州宪法在某些情况下保护私人财产上的言论自由，购物中心的行为明显违反了州宪法。”法院拒绝审理该行为是否违反联邦宪法的问题。
美国最高法院批准了调卷令（writ of certiorari），以审查州最高法院的这一判决。
美国最高法院应如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 维持州最高法院的判决。
zh-choices.B: 驳回调卷令，理由是其授予不当（improvidently granted）。
zh-choices.C: 将案件发回（remand）州最高法院。
zh-choices.D: 撤销州最高法院的判决。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法学: 司法审查

正确答案：B. 撤销已错误授予的调卷令。

核心要点：当州最高法院的判决明确基于充分且独立的州法依据时，美国最高法院（SCOTUS）无权审查该判决。

核心法律规则

充分且独立的州法依据原则 (Adequate and Independent State Grounds)

美国最高法院（SCOTUS）有权审查州最高法院基于联邦法作出的终审判决。然而，SCOTUS 无权审查基于充分且独立的州法依据的州法院判决。这意味着，如果州法院的判决是基于州法律，并且满足以下两个条件，SCOTUS 就没有管辖权：

  • 充分 (Adequate) – 州法律完全解决了该事项，以至于联邦法律的适用不会影响案件的结果。
  • 独立 (Independent) – 州法院在得出结论时，没有明确地通过引用联邦标准来纳入联邦标准。

如果调卷令 (writ of certiorari) 在这种情况下被错误地授予（即，不当地授予），SCOTUS 必须撤销该调卷令。

概念对比

特征 充分且独立的州法依据存在 联邦依据存在（无充分且独立州法依据）
SCOTUS 管辖权 无管辖权 有管辖权
州法院判决依据 州法律完全解决了争议事项；州法院未通过引用联邦标准来纳入联邦标准。 州法律未能完全解决争议；州法院纳入了联邦标准；或判决明确基于联邦法。
SCOTUS 结果 撤销调卷令（因无管辖权） 审查联邦问题

案件事实与分析逻辑

本案中，州最高法院的判决是基于充分的州法依据，因为适用联邦宪法不会影响州法院关于购物中心侵犯个人在州宪法下的言论自由权的裁决。即使联邦宪法不提供与州宪法相同的保护，州宪法本身也足以支持该判决，且联邦法的适用不会改变结果。

此外，该判决是基于独立的州法依据，因为法院拒绝审理购物中心行为是否违反联邦宪法的问题。这意味着州法院的判决完全独立于联邦法，没有通过引用联邦标准来纳入联邦标准。

*请注意：各州被允许承认超出美国宪法所赋予的个人权利。根据最高条款，联邦法律设定了一个州法律不能低于的底线，但它并未设定州法律不能超越的上限。

因此，由于州最高法院的判决明确基于充分且独立的州法依据，SCOTUS 缺乏审查该判决的管辖权。在这种情况下，SCOTUS 应该撤销已错误授予的调卷令。

概念图解

SCOTUS 对州法院判决的审查
(充分且独立的州法依据)
↓
判决是否基于充分且独立的州法依据？
↓
明确是
↓
无管辖权
不明确
↓
审查联邦问题
明确否
↓
审查联邦问题

考点陷阱与注意事项

陷阱警示：考生常误以为只要案件涉及联邦宪法问题，SCOTUS 就有权审查。然而，如果州法院的判决完全基于州法律，并且该州法律提供了与联邦法律相同或更广泛的保护，那么即使案件中提到了联邦问题，SCOTUS 也无权审查。关键在于州法依据是否“充分”且“独立”。

如果州法院的判决明确指出其裁决是基于州宪法，并且州宪法提供了比联邦宪法更广泛的权利，那么即使联邦宪法可能不会提供相同的保护，SCOTUS 也不能推翻州法院的判决，因为州法院的判决结果不会因联邦法律的适用而改变。

正确答案与干扰项排除

A. 维持州最高法院的判决。

当判决基于充分且独立的州法依据时，SCOTUS 没有管辖权来审查州法院判决的是非曲直，因此不能维持或推翻州最高法院的判决。它必须完全拒绝审查该判决。

B. 撤销已错误授予的调卷令。

这是正确的。本案中，州最高法院的判决明确基于充分且独立的州法依据。因此，SCOTUS 缺乏审查该判决的管辖权，必须撤销已错误授予的调卷令。

C. 将案件发回州最高法院。

当不清楚州法院的判决是基于州法还是联邦法时，允许将案件发回州法院。在这种情况下，SCOTUS 可以审理案件，裁决联邦问题，然后将案件发回州法院，以便解决任何州法律问题。但本案中，州法院的判决明确基于充分且独立的州法依据，因此不适用发回重审。

D. 推翻州最高法院的判决。

与选项 A 类似，当判决基于充分且独立的州法依据时，SCOTUS 没有管辖权来审查州法院判决的是非曲直，因此不能推翻州最高法院的决定。它必须完全拒绝审查该判决。

考试技巧

快速判断：在 MBE 考试中，如果题目明确指出州法院的判决是基于州宪法或州法律，并且州法院明确拒绝审理联邦问题，或者州法律提供了比联邦法更广泛的保护，那么几乎可以肯定 SCOTUS 将因“充分且独立的州法依据”而没有管辖权，并会撤销调卷令。SCOTUS 关注的是联邦法律问题，而不是州法律问题。

参考文献

Harris v. Reed, 489 U.S. 225, 260 (1989) (裁定美国最高法院缺乏管辖权审查基于充分且独立的州法依据的州法院判决)。

科目

宪法学 (Constitutional Law)

章节

司法审查 (Judicial Review)

主题

充分且独立的州法依据 (Adequate and Independent State Grounds)

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute, applicable to all public and private employers, makes discrimination against persons with a certain disability in the hiring or firing of employees illegal. It also provides for a civil action for damages against the offending employer. The statute contains a clear statement of Congressional intent to abrogate state immunity pursuant to its powers under the Fourteenth Amendment.
An employee sued her employer in federal court for violation of this statute and sought relief in the form of retroactive money damages. The employer, a state agency, moved to dismiss the action as constitutionally prohibited. The employee conceded that the state agency's acts, like most historical acts of discrimination against individuals with this particular disability, were rationally related to a legitimate government purpose.
Should the court dismiss the action on constitutional grounds?

choices.A: No, because Congress enacted the statute pursuant to its constitutional power under the Enabling Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.B: No, because Congress was acting pursuant to its power under the Commerce Clause.
choices.C: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prevents the recovery of retroactive money damages by citizens against a state agency.
choices.D: Yes, because the state agency's actions did not violate the Equal Protection Clause.

questions.explanation:
Eleventh Amendment
(state immunity from suit in federal court)
Immunity
  • Suit brought by private party or foreign government
  • Suit against state official violating state law
  • Exceptions:
    • State consents to suit
    • Immunity removed by 13th, 14th, or 15th Amendment
    • State official sued for injunctive or declaratory relief for alleged constitutional violation
    • Damages to be paid by state officer personally (not state treasury)
    • State official sued for prospective (not retroactive) damages to be paid by state treasury
No
immunity
  • Suit brought by United States or other state
  • Suit against local government (eg, counties, municipalities)
  • Bankruptcy proceedings
  • Eminent domain proceedings
  • Suits permitted by Congress pursuant to its powers over war & armed forces

The Eleventh Amendment generally forbids the federal courts from hearing private suits for damages against the states. Congress typically cannot override this ban unless it is clearly acting to enforce the Civil War Amendments, including acting under the Fourteenth Amendment, Section 5 Enabling Clause. When enforcing such amendments, Congress may enact appropriate remedial legislation expressly subjecting the states to private suits for damages in federal court.

Here, the federal statute unambiguously states Congress's intent to abrogate state immunity for discrimination against persons with a certain disability in public and private employers' hiring and firing practices. Congress enacted this statute pursuant to its constitutional power under the Enabling Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment. Therefore, the court should not dismiss the action on constitutional grounds.

(Choice B) Congress may abrogate a state's sovereign immunity pursuant to the Enabling Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to enforce rights created by the remedial provisions of the Civil War Amendments. However, it cannot abrogate state sovereign immunity under the Commerce Clause.

(Choice C) Retroactive damages are not available in suits against state officials if the damages are to be paid by the state treasury (not seen here). But here, the Enabling Clause allows Congress to enact appropriate remedial legislation subjecting the state and its agencies to suits for retroactive and prospective damages.

(Choice D) Whether the state agency's actions violated the Equal Protection Clause is a question on the merits of the employee's suit—not grounds to dismiss the action based on the Eleventh Amendment.

📌 Educational Objective

Congress cannot override the Eleventh Amendment. But when Congress is clearly acting to enforce the Civil War Amendments (e.g., acting under the Fourteenth Amendment Enabling Clause), it may enact appropriate remedial legislation expressly subjecting the states to private suits for damages in federal court.

📚 References
  • Fitzpatrick v. Bitzer, 427 U.S. 445 (1976) (holding that Congress enforcement of the Fourteenth Amendment under the Enabling Clause can override state sovereign immunity under the Eleventh Amendment).
questions.zh-question:
一项联邦法规，适用于所有公共和私人雇主，规定在雇佣或解雇员工时歧视特定残疾人是非法的。它还规定了针对违规雇主提起损害赔偿民事诉讼的权利。该法规明确声明国会有意根据其在《第十四修正案》（Fourteenth Amendment）下的权力废除州主权豁免。
一名员工在联邦法院起诉其雇主违反该法规，并寻求追溯性金钱损害赔偿。雇主，一个州机构，动议驳回该诉讼，理由是其受到宪法禁止。员工承认，该州机构的行为，像大多数历史上针对该特定残疾人的歧视行为一样，与合法的政府目的有合理关联。
法院是否应以宪法理由驳回该诉讼？

zh-choices.A: 不应驳回，因为国会是根据其在《第十四修正案》的《授权条款》（Enabling Clause）下的宪法权力颁布该法规的。
zh-choices.B: 不应驳回，因为国会是根据其在《商业条款》（Commerce Clause）下的权力行事的。
zh-choices.C: 应驳回，因为《第十一修正案》（Eleventh Amendment）禁止公民向州机构追溯性地追讨金钱损害赔偿。
zh-choices.D: 应驳回，因为该州机构的行为并未违反《平等保护条款》（Equal Protection Clause）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法学: 司法审查

正确答案: A

国会根据第十四修正案的授权条款制定法律，可以废除州的第十一修正案主权豁免权，允许公民对州机构提起损害赔偿诉讼。

核心法律规则

第十一修正案与国会废除州主权豁免权

  • 第十一修正案 通常禁止联邦法院审理私人针对州提起的损害赔偿诉讼，确立了州主权豁免权。
  • 然而，国会可以根据其在 第十四修正案第5节授权条款 (Enabling Clause) 下的权力，废除州的第十一修正案豁免权。
  • 当国会根据第十四修正案行事时，它可以制定适当的补救性立法，明确规定州可以被私人起诉以追究损害赔偿责任。
  • 这种权力是独特的，不同于国会根据《商业条款》等其他条款行使的权力，后者通常不能废除州的损害赔偿豁免权。

第十一修正案豁免权概览

第十一修正案 (州在联邦法院免受诉讼的豁免权)
豁免 (Immunity)
  • 私人或外国政府提起的诉讼
  • 针对违反州法律的州官员提起的诉讼
  • 例外情况:
    • 州同意被起诉
    • 第十三、十四或十五修正案废除了豁免权
    • 州官员因涉嫌违反宪法被起诉，要求禁令性或宣告性救济
    • 损害赔偿由州官员个人支付 (而非州财政)
    • 州官员因未来 (非追溯性) 损害赔偿被起诉，由州财政支付
无豁免 (No Immunity)
  • 美国政府或其他州提起的诉讼
  • 针对地方政府 (例如，县、市) 提起的诉讼
  • 破产程序
  • 征用权程序
  • 国会根据其战争和武装部队权力允许的诉讼

事实与适用逻辑

本案中，一项联邦法规禁止对残疾人进行歧视，并允许针对违规雇主（包括州机构）提起民事损害赔偿诉讼。该法规明确声明国会意图根据其在第十四修正案下的权力废除州豁免权。

根据 第十四修正案第5节授权条款，国会拥有权力通过适当的立法来执行该修正案的规定。最高法院在 Fitzpatrick v. Bitzer 案中明确指出，国会根据第十四修正案行事时，可以废除州的第十一修正案主权豁免权，从而允许公民在联邦法院对州提起损害赔偿诉讼。

尽管雇员承认州机构的行为可能与合法的政府目的合理相关（暗示可能不直接违反平等保护条款的“合理基础”标准），但这并不妨碍国会根据第十四修正案第5节制定法律来禁止此类行为并废除州豁免权。国会在此条款下的权力是补救性的，可以禁止那些本身不违宪但有助于防止或补救宪法侵犯的行为，只要其立法是“相称且适当”的。

因此，由于国会明确根据第十四修正案的授权条款行事，法院不应以宪法豁免权为由驳回诉讼。

国会废除州主权豁免权的路径

第十一修正案
➜
州主权豁免权 (一般规则)

第十四修正案第5节授权条款
➜
国会执行权力
➜
废除州豁免权 (允许损害赔偿诉讼)

陷阱警示: 混淆国会权力来源

MBE常考的一个陷阱是混淆国会根据不同宪法条款行使的权力对州主权豁免权的影响。虽然国会根据 《商业条款》 (Commerce Clause) 通常不能废除州的第十一修正案豁免权以允许私人提起损害赔偿诉讼（参见 Seminole Tribe v. Florida），但 第十四修正案第5节授权条款 是一个重要的例外。务必记住，只有当国会明确根据第十四修正案行事时，它才能有效地废除州的主权豁免权，允许私人追溯性地向州寻求损害赔偿。

正确答案与干扰项排除

A. 不应驳回，因为国会根据第十四修正案的授权条款制定了该法规。

正确。 国会根据第十四修正案第5节授权条款行事时，可以废除州的主权豁免权，允许私人对州提起损害赔偿诉讼。本案中的联邦法规明确声明了国会的这一意图。

B. 不应驳回，因为国会是根据其在《商业条款》下的权力行事。

错误。 国会根据《商业条款》行事时，通常不能废除州的第十一修正案豁免权，以允许私人对州提起损害赔偿诉讼。这是《商业条款》与第十四修正案授权条款之间的一个关键区别。

C. 应驳回，因为第十一修正案阻止公民向州机构追回追溯性金钱损害赔偿。

错误。 尽管第十一修正案通常会阻止追溯性金钱损害赔偿，但当国会根据第十四修正案第5节授权条款明确废除豁免权时，此规则有一个重要例外。本案中，国会正是这样做的。

D. 应驳回，因为州机构的行为并未违反《平等保护条款》。

错误。 州机构行为是否违反《平等保护条款》是案件实体问题，与法院是否有管辖权审理此案（即州主权豁免权问题）无关。国会根据第十四修正案第5节的权力，可以禁止那些本身不构成宪法违宪但有助于防止或补救宪法违宪的行为，只要其立法是“相称且适当”的。因此，即使州的行为不直接违反《平等保护条款》的合理基础标准，国会仍可立法禁止并废除豁免权。

考试技巧

在MBE考试中，当遇到涉及州主权豁免权的问题时，请立即检查国会立法所依据的宪法权力来源。如果国会明确依据 第十四修正案第5节授权条款 行事，那么它通常可以有效地废除州的第十一修正案豁免权，允许私人提起损害赔偿诉讼。这是第十一修正案规则的一个核心例外。

参考文献

  • Fitzpatrick v. Bitzer, 427 U.S. 445 (1976) (判决国会根据第十四修正案的授权条款执行法律时，可以废除第十一修正案下的州主权豁免权)。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute enacted pursuant to the power of Congress to enforce the Fourteenth Amendment prohibits any state from requiring any of its employees to retire from state employment solely because of their age. The statute expressly authorizes employees required by a state to retire from state employment solely because of their age to sue the state government in federal district court for any damages resulting from that state action.
On the basis of this federal statute, a retiree sues State X in federal district court. State X moves to dismiss the suit on the ground that Congress lacks authority to authorize such suits against a state.
Which of the following is the strongest argument that the retiree can offer in opposition to the state's motion to dismiss this suit?

choices.A: When Congress exercises power vested in it by any provision of the Constitution, Congress has unlimited authority to authorize private actions for damages against a state.
choices.B: When Congress exercises power vested in it by the Fourteenth Amendment, Congress may enact appropriate remedial legislation expressly subjecting the states to private suits for damages in federal court.
choices.C: While the Eleventh Amendment applies to suits in federal court by citizens of one state against another state, it does not apply to such suits by citizens against their own states.
choices.D: While the Eleventh Amendment restrains the federal judiciary, that amendment does not limit the power of Congress to modify the sovereign immunity of the states.

questions.explanation:
Eleventh Amendment
(state immunity from suit in federal court)
Immunity
  • Suit brought by private party or foreign government
  • Suit against state official violating state law
  • Exceptions:
    • State consents to suit
    • Immunity removed by 13th, 14th, or 15th Amendment
    • State official sued for injunctive or declaratory relief for alleged constitutional violation
    • Damages to be paid by state officer personally (not state treasury)
    • State official sued for prospective (not retroactive) damages to be paid by state treasury
No immunity
  • Suit brought by United States or other state
  • Suit against local government (eg, counties, municipalities)
  • Bankruptcy proceedings
  • Eminent domain proceedings
  • Suits permitted by Congress pursuant to its powers over war & armed forces

The Eleventh Amendment generally forbids the federal courts from hearing private suits for damages against the states. Congress cannot override this ban, even to exercise one of its constitutionally enumerated powers (Choices A & D). But there is a narrow exception to this rule when Congress is clearly acting to enforce the Civil War Amendments (eg, Fourteenth Amendment—as seen here). In that case, it may enact appropriate remedial legislation expressly subjecting the states to private suits for damages in federal court.

(Choice C) The Eleventh Amendment applies to all private suits for damages against the states—including suits by citizens against their own state. But it does not bar Congress from authorizing such suits as a means of enforcing the Civil War Amendments.

📌 Educational Objective

The Eleventh Amendment generally forbids the federal courts from hearing private suits for damages against the states. But Congress can authorize such suits when it is clearly acting to enforce the Civil War Amendments (ie, Thirteenth, Fourteenth, and Fifteenth Amendments).

📚 References
  • United States v. Georgia, 546 U.S. 151, 158–59 (2006) (explaining that the Fourteenth Amendment allows Congress to abrogate state sovereign immunity by authorizing private suits for damages against the states).

一项根据国会执行 Fourteenth Amendment 的权力而制定的联邦法规，禁止任何州仅因年龄原因要求其任何雇员从州政府部门退休。该法规明确授权因年龄原因被州政府要求退休的雇员，可就该州行为造成的任何损害，在联邦地区法院向州政府提起诉讼。

zh-choices.C: 虽然 Eleventh Amendment 适用于一个州的公民在联邦法院对另一个州提起的诉讼，但它不适用于公民对本州提起的此类诉讼。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Sovereign Immunity
正确答案：选项 B

这是最强有力的论点：当国会行使 Fourteenth Amendment（第十四修正案）授予的权力时，可以明确废除各州的主权豁免权。

核心法律规则解析

1. 第十一修正案 (11th Amendment) 的一般原则

通常情况下，Eleventh Amendment 禁止联邦法院审理私人针对“州”（State）的损害赔偿诉讼。这就是所谓的州主权豁免 (State Sovereign Immunity)。

2. 国会的废除权 (Abrogation)

国会想要废除各州的这种豁免权，必须满足两个条件：

  • 明确表达 (Unequivocally express)： 国会必须在立法中明确表示要允许针对州的诉讼。
  • 合法的权力来源 (Valid source of power)： 这是本题的关键。

3. 权力来源的区别 (The Critical Distinction)

这是 MBE 宪法部分的高频考点，请务必区分：

  • ❌ Article I Powers (如 Commerce Clause): 国会不能利用第一条的权力（如商务条款）来废除第十一修正案的豁免权。
    Seminole Tribe v. Florida (1996)
  • ✅ 14th Amendment, Section 5: 国会可以利用第十四修正案第 5 款（执行条款）来废除豁免权。因为第十四修正案是在第十一修正案之后通过的，它从根本上改变了联邦与州权力的平衡。
    Fitzpatrick v. Bitzer (1976)
本题逻辑分析

题目中明确指出：

  1. 该法规是根据国会执行 Fourteenth Amendment 的权力制定的。
  2. 该法规明确授权 (expressly authorizes) 雇员起诉州政府。

因此，退休人员最有力的反驳就是指出国会是在行使第十四修正案的权力，这是废除州主权豁免的合法途径。

为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A 错误： 声称国会行使“任何”宪法权力都能废除豁免权是错误的。如前所述，行使 Article I (如商务条款) 的权力是无效的。
选项 C 错误： 这是一个常见的陷阱。虽然第十一修正案的文本只提到了“他州公民”，但最高法院在 Hans v. Louisiana (1890) 中确立，主权豁免原则同样禁止本州公民在联邦法院起诉自己的州。
选项 D 错误： 这过于宽泛。第十一修正案确实限制了国会修改主权豁免的权力（限制了国会使用 Article I powers），除非国会使用的是第十四修正案的权力。

Congress passed a statute that expressly authorizes suits for damages in federal courts against state governments that violate federal copyright laws.
A photographer sued a state in a federal district court for damages pursuant to the federal statute. The photographer claimed that the state published her copyrighted photographs and videos on its website without her permission. The state has moved to dismiss the photographer's suit.

choices.C: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits the action for damages against the state in federal court.
choices.D: Yes, because the Tenth Amendment prohibits the federal government from compelling states to act.

  • Suits permitted by Congress pursuant to its powers over war & armed forces

The Eleventh Amendment generally prohibits private parties and foreign governments from suing a state for money damages or equitable relief in federal court. Congress can abrogate (i.e., repeal) this immunity if it is clearly acting to enforce a Civil War Amendment—i.e., the Thirteenth, Fourteenth, or Fifteenth Amendment (not seen here). Congress may then enact appropriate remedial legislation expressly subjecting the states to private suits for damages in federal court.

However, Congress cannot abrogate a state's Eleventh Amendment immunity through its other powers.* This includes its Article I power to enact laws protecting copyrighted materials (Choice A). This also includes its power under Articles I and III to regulate the jurisdiction of the federal courts (Choice B). Therefore, the court will likely grant the state's motion to dismiss the photographer's suit pursuant to the Eleventh Amendment.

*The U.S. Supreme Court has held that the plan of the Constitutional Convention included certain waivers of sovereign immunity to which all states implicitly consented when they joined the United States—e.g., bankruptcy proceedings, eminent domain proceedings, suits permitted by Congress pursuant to its powers over war and the armed forces. In these situations, no congressional abrogation is necessary.

(Choice D) The Tenth Amendment prohibits the federal government from compelling states to enact state laws or enforce federal laws. However, states can be subjected to suits for damages in federal court if Congress validly abrogated state immunity (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The Eleventh Amendment generally grants states immunity from suits for damages. Congress can abrogate this immunity when it clearly acts to enforce a Civil War Amendment but cannot do so through its other powers—e.g., its powers to protect copyrights and regulate federal court jurisdiction.

📚 References
  • Allen v. Cooper, 140 S. Ct. 994, 1007 (2020) (holding that Congress cannot abrogate the states' Eleventh Amendment immunity through the Article I copyright clause).

国会通过了一项法规，明确授权可在联邦法院对违反联邦版权法的州政府提起损害赔偿诉讼。

一位摄影师依据该联邦法规，在联邦地区法院起诉一个州，要求损害赔偿。该摄影师声称，该州未经其许可，在其网站上发布了她拥有版权的照片和视频。该州已提出动议，请求驳回该摄影师的诉讼。

法院是否应批准该州的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为宪法第一条 (Article I) 授予国会制定保护版权材料的法律的权力。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为宪法第一条 (Article I) 和第三条 (Article III) 授予国会规范联邦法院管辖权和程序的权力。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为宪法第十一修正案 (Eleventh Amendment) 禁止在联邦法院对州提起的损害赔偿诉讼。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为宪法第十修正案 (Tenth Amendment) 禁止联邦政府强迫州采取行动。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法：第十一修正案与主权豁免
正确答案：C

法院应批准州的动议，因为第十一修正案 (Eleventh Amendment) 禁止在联邦法院对州提起损害赔偿诉讼。

⚖️ 核心考点：主权豁免 (Sovereign Immunity)

第十一修正案确立了一项基本原则：州 (States) 享有主权豁免权。这意味着，未经州同意，私人当事人（如本案中的摄影师）不能在联邦法院起诉州政府要求金钱赔偿。

虽然国会 (Congress) 有权废除 (Abrogate) 这种豁免权，但必须同时满足两个条件：

  1. 国会必须明确表达废除豁免权的意图；且
  2. 国会必须依据有效的宪法权力行事。
🚫 陷阱：国会权力的来源

这是本题最大的考点。国会依据什么权力可以废除州的豁免权？

  • ❌ 宪法第一条 (Article I) 权力： 最高法院已裁定，国会不能利用 Article I 的权力（如商业条款、版权条款）来废除州的第十一修正案豁免权。
  • ✅ 第十四修正案 (14th Amendment) 第5款： 国会可以利用此条款（执行条款）废除豁免权，前提是该立法是为了防止或补救对宪法权利的侵犯。
Allen v. Cooper (2020)

这道题几乎是该判例的翻版。最高法院在该案中明确裁定：国会无权依据 Article I 的版权条款 (Copyright Clause) 废除各州在版权侵权诉讼中的主权豁免权。

🔍 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A 错误：
虽然 Article I 确实授予国会制定版权法的权力，但这属于 Article I 权力。根据 Seminole Tribe 和 Allen v. Cooper 判例，Article I 权力不足以废除州的宪法豁免权。

选项 B 错误：
国会规范联邦法院管辖权的权力（Article III）也不能用来规避第十一修正案的宪法限制。

选项 D 错误：
虽然第十修正案 (Tenth Amendment) 涉及反强迫原则 (Anti-Commandeering)，但本案的核心障碍是主权豁免 (Sovereign Immunity)，这是第十一修正案的范畴，而非第十修正案。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

当你在 MBE 宪法题中看到：

  1. 原告是私人 (Private Party)；
  2. 被告是州 (State)；
  3. 诉讼在联邦法院 (Federal Court)；
  4. 要求金钱赔偿 (Money Damages)；

你的第一反应应该是：第十一修正案禁止此诉讼，除非有非常特殊的例外（如依据第14修正案的有效立法，或州明确放弃豁免）。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Federal officials from the Environmental Protection Agency sought an injunction in federal court to prevent the owner of a hazardous waste facility from illegally discharging pollution from the facility into a river. Shortly before trial, the owner temporarily closed the facility for routine maintenance, which halted the discharge of pollutants into the river. The owner then filed a motion to dismiss the action as moot.
Should the court grant the owner's motion to dismiss?

choices.A: No, because a live controversy existed at the time the suit was filed.
choices.B: No, because the owner may resume polluting the river at any time.
choices.C: Yes, because the injunction sought by the government would have a prospective effect.
choices.D: Yes, because the owner is no longer discharging pollutants in the river.

questions.explanation:
Ripeness v. Mootness
Ripe (too soon) Action will not be heard until plaintiff has experienced actual injury or imminent threat thereof
Moot (too late) Action will be dismissed if further proceedings would have no effect unless:
  • plaintiff's harm is capable of repetition yet evading review (eg, pregnancy)
  • defendant voluntarily stops action but can resume it anytime
  • plaintiff is named plaintiff in class action & claims of unnamed plaintiffs are still viable

Federal courts have the power to decide actual cases and controversies (i.e., disputes that are capable of judicial resolution). If an actual case or controversy no longer exists because circumstances have changed and further legal proceedings would have no effect, then the case is moot and will be dismissed. But a court will not dismiss a case as moot if:

  • the defendant voluntarily ceased the challenged conduct after litigation began but
  • it is reasonable to expect that the defendant may resume that conduct at any time.

Here, federal officials sought an injunction in federal court to stop the facility owner from polluting the river. Although the owner is no longer discharging pollutants into the river, this voluntary cessation occurred after litigation began and is merely a closure for routine maintenance. It is therefore reasonable to expect that the owner may resume discharging pollutants after the facility reopens (Choice D). This means that the case is not moot, and the owner's motion to dismiss should be denied.

(Choice A) A live case or controversy must exist at every stage of the proceeding—not just when the suit is filed.

(Choice C) Although the government seeks to enjoin future illegal pollution, the owner's voluntary cessation of that illegal conduct does not moot this action because it is reasonable to assume that the illegal conduct will resume.

📌 Educational Objective

When an actual case or controversy no longer exists, a case will generally be dismissed as moot. However, such a dismissal will not occur if (1) the defendant voluntarily ceased the challenged conduct after litigation began but (2) it is reasonable to expect that the defendant may resume that conduct at any time.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case-or-controversy requirement).
  • Turner v. Rogers, 564 U.S. 431, 439–40 (2011) (explaining the mootness doctrine and its exceptions).
questions.zh-question: 联邦环境保护局 (Environmental Protection Agency, EPA) 的联邦官员在联邦法院寻求禁令 (injunction)，以阻止一家危险废物处理设施的所有者将污染物从该设施非法排入一条河流。庭审前不久，该所有者暂时关闭了该设施进行例行维护，这停止了污染物排入河流。该所有者随后提出动议，要求以案件已“无实际争议” (moot) 为由驳回诉讼。法院是否应批准该所有者的驳回动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为在提起诉讼时存在一个“有实际争议” (live controversy)。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为该所有者可能随时恢复污染河流。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为政府寻求的禁令将具有“前瞻性效力” (prospective effect)。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为该所有者不再向河流排放污染物。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法：司法审查

正确答案：B
法院不应驳回所有者的动议，因为所有者随时可能恢复污染河流的行为。

核心法律规则：可诉性原则 (Mootness Doctrine)

根据美国宪法第三条，联邦法院的司法权仅限于“案件和争议” (actual cases and controversies)。这意味着法院只能审理那些存在真实、具体争议的案件，且该争议在诉讼的各个阶段都必须是“活的” (live)。如果争议在诉讼过程中消失，案件通常会被驳回，理由是其已变为 “可诉性” (moot)。

然而，可诉性原则存在一些重要例外，即使争议表面上已不复存在，法院仍可能继续审理案件。其中一个关键例外是：

  • 当被告在诉讼开始后 自愿停止 (voluntarily ceased) 了被挑战的行为，但 合理预期 (reasonable to expect) 其随时可能 恢复 (resume) 该行为时，案件不会被视为可诉。

其他例外包括：

  • 原告的伤害具有 重复性但又规避审查 (capable of repetition yet evading review) 的特点（例如，怀孕案件）。
  • 在集体诉讼中，即使具名原告的个人索赔已变为可诉，但 未具名原告的索赔仍然存在 (claims of unnamed plaintiffs are still viable)。

概念比较：诉讼成熟度 (Ripeness) 与可诉性 (Mootness)

概念 描述
诉讼成熟度 (Ripeness)
(为时过早)		 在原告尚未经历实际伤害或迫在眉睫的威胁之前，法院不会审理该诉讼。
可诉性 (Mootness)
(为时过晚)		 如果进一步的诉讼程序将不再产生任何实际影响，案件将被驳回，除非存在例外情况。

案情分析与法律适用

第一步：识别核心争议点

本案的核心争议点是，尽管被告（设施所有者）已暂时停止排放污染物，但其自愿停止行为是否使联邦环保局 (EPA) 寻求禁令的诉讼变得 可诉 (moot)。

第二步：适用可诉性原则的例外

根据可诉性原则的例外，如果被告在诉讼开始后自愿停止了被挑战的行为，但合理预期其随时可能恢复该行为，则案件不会被视为可诉。

  • 事实：设施所有者在诉讼开始后，因“例行维护”而暂时关闭设施，从而停止了污染物的排放。
  • 分析：“例行维护”通常是临时性的，且设施所有者可以随时重新开放设施并恢复排放污染物。因此，存在 合理预期 (reasonable to expect) 所有者可能恢复其非法行为。

第三步：得出结论

由于存在合理预期所有者会恢复污染行为，法院不应将此案视为可诉。环保局寻求禁令的目的正是为了防止未来的污染，这仍然是一个“活的”争议。

可诉性判断流程图

是否存在“活的”案件或争议？
↓
争议是否在诉讼过程中消失？
↓
被告是否自愿停止了被挑战的行为？
↓
合理预期被告会恢复该行为吗？
↓
是 → 案件不 moot (继续审理)
否 → 案件 moot (驳回)

MBE 考点陷阱提示

MBE 考试中，关于可诉性原则的常见陷阱是混淆“自愿停止”与“争议彻底消失”。仅仅因为被告暂时停止了非法行为，并不意味着案件就自动变为可诉。关键在于判断被告是否可能随时恢复该行为，尤其当停止行为是“自愿”且“临时性”时。如果存在恢复的可能性，法院通常会认为争议仍然存在，从而拒绝驳回。

正确答案与干扰项排除

B. 不，因为所有者随时可能恢复污染河流的行为。

【正确】这是可诉性原则的一个重要例外。当被告自愿停止了被挑战的行为，但合理预期其随时可能恢复该行为时，案件不会被视为可诉。本案中，所有者因“例行维护”而暂时关闭设施，这表明其随时可能重新开放并恢复污染，因此争议仍然“活的”。

A. 不，因为在诉讼提起时存在真实的争议。

【错误】虽然在诉讼提起时存在真实的争议是必要的（满足 诉讼成熟度 (ripeness) 要求），但可诉性原则要求争议在诉讼的 各个阶段 (all stages) 都必须是“活的”。仅仅在提起时存在争议不足以阻止案件在后续阶段因争议消失而变为可诉。此选项未能抓住可诉性原则的关键点，即争议的持续性。

C. 是，因为政府寻求的禁令将具有前瞻性效果。

【错误】政府寻求禁令的目的通常就是为了防止未来的伤害，这本身就具有前瞻性。如果案件已变为可诉，即使禁令具有前瞻性，法院也缺乏审理该案件的宪法权力。这个选项混淆了禁令的性质与可诉性原则的适用条件。禁令的前瞻性恰恰是法院继续审理的理由，如果争议未消失的话。

D. 是，因为所有者不再排放污染物。

【错误】这个选项直接忽略了可诉性原则的“自愿停止但可能恢复”的例外。虽然所有者目前不再排放污染物，但这只是因为“例行维护”导致的暂时性停止。如果法院因此驳回案件，所有者可以在维护结束后立即恢复污染，从而规避司法审查。因此，仅仅停止排放不足以使案件变为可诉。

MBE 考试技巧

在判断可诉性时，要特别留意被告的“自愿停止”行为。如果被告是自愿停止且有合理可能性恢复被挑战的行为，那么案件通常 不会 被视为可诉。这通常发生在被告为了规避诉讼而暂时停止行为的情况下。记住，联邦法院的权力是有限的，但它们会确保其判决能够对实际争议产生实际影响，而不是让被告通过临时行为逃避审查。

参考文献

  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case-or-controversy requirement)
  • Turner v. Rogers, 564 U.S. 431, 439–40 (2011) (explaining the mootness doctrine and its exceptions)

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The United States had long recognized the ruling faction in a foreign country as that country's government, despite an ongoing civil war. Throughout the civil war, the ruling faction controlled the majority of the country's territory, and the United States afforded diplomatic immunity to the ambassador representing the ruling faction.
A newly elected President of the United States decided to recognize a rebel group as the government of the foreign country and notified the ambassador from the ruling faction that she must leave the United States within 10 days. The ambassador filed an action in federal district court for a declaration that the ruling faction was the true government of the foreign country and for an injunction against enforcement of the President's order that she leave the United States. The United States has moved to dismiss the action.
If the court dismisses the action, what will be the most likely reason?

choices.A: The action involves a nonjusticiable political question.
choices.B: The action is not ripe.
choices.C: The action is within the original jurisdiction of the U.S. Supreme Court.
choices.D: The ambassador does not have standing.

questions.explanation:
Article III of the Constitution grants federal courts the power to decide actual cases and controversies. But the political-question doctrine prohibits federal courts from adjudicating political questions—ie, issues that (1) the Constitution reserves to the legislative and executive branches or (2) lack judicially discoverable and manageable standards for resolution. When this occurs, the federal court must dismiss the suit.

Here, the ambassador's suit for a declaratory judgment and an injunction concerned the President's recognition of a rebel group as the foreign country's true government. But such power is reserved to the executive branch under the Constitution, and there are no standards to help a court resolve this dispute. Therefore, the court will most likely dismiss this action because it involves a nonjusticiable political question.

(Choice B) Under Article III's case-or-controversy requirement, a suit must be ripe for adjudication. This means that the plaintiff must have suffered actual harm or an immediate threat thereof. Here, the ambassador's action is ripe because she has been ordered to leave the U.S. within 10 days (immediate threat of harm).

(Choice C) The U.S. Supreme Court has original jurisdiction over cases affecting ambassadors, so the ambassador's suit could have been filed directly in the Supreme Court. But original jurisdiction over ambassadors is not exclusive, so a lower federal court could also adjudicate this case if it was justiciable.

(Choice D) The ambassador does have standing because she suffered an injury-in-fact (expulsion) that was caused by the challenged action (President's order) and is redressable by the remedy sought (injunction).

📌 Educational Objective

Under the political-question doctrine, federal courts cannot decide issues that (1) the Constitution reserves to the other branches of government or (2) lack judicially discoverable and manageable standards for resolution. Therefore, suits presenting these nonjusticiable political questions must be dismissed.

📚 References
  • Jones v. United States, 137 U.S. 202, 212 (1890) (stating that the recognition of a foreign government and its representatives is a nonjusticiable political question).
  • Baker v. Carr, 369 U.S. 186, 210–17 (1962) (discussing the political-question doctrine).
  • 32 Am. Jur. 2d Fed. Courts § 574 (2019) (listing examples of political questions).

美国长期以来承认某外国的执政派系为该国政府，尽管该国持续存在内战。在整个内战期间，该执政派系控制了该国大部分领土，且美国给予代表该执政派系的大使外交豁免权。

新当选的美国总统决定承认一个叛乱团体为该外国的政府，并通知来自执政派系的大使，她必须在10天内离开美国。该大使向联邦地区法院提起诉讼，请求宣告执政派系为该外国的合法政府，并请求签发禁令，禁止执行总统要求她离开美国的命令。美国政府已动议驳回此诉讼。

如果法院驳回此诉讼，最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: 该诉讼涉及一个不可由法院审理的政治问题。
zh-choices.B: 该诉讼尚未成熟。
zh-choices.C: 该诉讼属于美国最高法院的初始管辖权范围。
zh-choices.D: 该大使不具备诉讼资格。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法学：司法审查与政治问题
正确答案 A 政治问题原则 (Political Question Doctrine)

本题的核心考点是联邦法院的可司法性 (Justiciability)，具体涉及政治问题原则 (Political Question Doctrine)。

法律依据

根据美国最高法院在 Baker v. Carr (1962) 案中确立的标准，如果一个案件表现出以下特征，则属于不可由法院审理的“政治问题”：

1. 宪法文本明确将该问题交给其他政府部门处理（Textually demonstrable constitutional commitment）；
2. 缺乏可由司法发现和管理的解决标准（Lack of judicially discoverable and manageable standards）。
本案分析

本案涉及承认外国政府 (Recognition of Foreign Governments) 的权力。

宪法第二条第三款（Article II, Section 3）规定总统有权“接见大使和其他公使”（Receive Ambassadors）。最高法院长期以来（如在 Zivotofsky v. Kerry 案中确认）将此解释为总统拥有承认外国政府的专属权力。

因此，承认哪个派系为合法政府是行政部门（Executive Branch）的特权，法院没有宪法权力，也没有合适的法律标准来干涉这一外交决策。法院必须驳回此案。

干扰项排除
选项 B：成熟度 (Ripeness)

错误。成熟度要求原告面临实际的伤害或即刻的威胁。本案中，大使已被命令在10天内离境，伤害迫在眉睫，因此案件已经成熟。

选项 C：最高法院初始管辖权 (Original Jurisdiction)

错误。虽然宪法规定最高法院对涉及大使的案件拥有初始管辖权，但这并非专属管辖权 (Exclusive Jurisdiction)。国会已授权联邦地区法院对此类案件拥有并发管辖权 (Concurrent Jurisdiction)。

选项 D：诉讼资格 (Standing)

错误。大使面临被驱逐出境，这构成了具体的“事实损害” (Injury-in-fact)，且该损害由总统命令导致并可由法院禁令救济。她具备诉讼资格，只是法院因“政治问题”无法审理该事项。

在宪法题中，如果你看到以下关键词，极大概率涉及政治问题原则，法院通常会驳回起诉：

  • 外交事务 (Foreign Affairs)：如承认国家、条约废除。
  • 弹劾程序 (Impeachment Process)：参议院如何审判弹劾案。
  • 共和政体条款 (Republican Form of Government)：涉及宪法第四条第四款的保障。
  • 党派不公划界 (Partisan Gerrymandering)：最高法院近期裁定这属于政治问题（Rucho v. Common Cause）。

口诀：涉及总统外交特权或国会内部程序，法院通常“绕道走”。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
In order to reduce the federal deficit, Congress passed, and the President signed into law, a statute that grants the President line-item veto power. Pursuant to this power, the President has the authority to cancel specific spending and tax-benefit measures that have been enacted into law.
Several members of Congress who voted against the legislation have sued the appropriate federal officials in a federal district court. The members of Congress claim that the statute is unconstitutional because it violates the requirements of the federal legislative process. The federal officials move to dismiss the suit.
Which of the following is the most appropriate basis for the court to dismiss this suit?

choices.A: The Eleventh Amendment bars suits of this kind in federal court.
choices.B: The members of Congress do not have standing.
choices.C: The suit presents a nonjusticiable political question.
choices.D: The U.S. Supreme Court has exclusive jurisdiction over the action.

questions.explanation:
Article III standing
(suing on one's own behalf)
General rule Plaintiff must prove:
  • injury-in-fact — concrete & particularized harm (actual or imminent)
  • causation — harm traceable to defendant's conduct AND
  • redressability — favorable judicial decision can remedy harm
Citizen No standing as mere citizen
Legislator Must prove personal stake in dispute & concrete injury to challenge constitutionality of government action
Taxpayer Standing to challenge taxes owed—but not government spending unless:
  • challenging legislation enacted under taxing & spending power AND
  • legislation exceeds limits imposed by establishment clause

Federal courts can only hear suits in which the plaintiff has standing—ie, a personal stake in the outcome of the case. A federal or state legislator has standing to challenge the constitutionality of government action in the rare instance that the action caused the legislator personal and concrete harm—eg, by nullifying the legislator's vote. Institutional, abstract harm shared equally by all legislators in that respective body does not confer standing.

Here, several members of Congress have challenged the constitutionality of the federal statute. However, the statute has not caused the members to suffer personal and concrete injuries since they were able to vote against the statute and can vote to repeal it in the future. Instead, they are asserting institutional, abstract harm that is shared equally by all other members of Congress. Therefore, the most appropriate basis to dismiss the suit is that the members of Congress lack standing.*

*In Clinton v. City of New York, the U.S. Supreme Court held that plaintiffs who would lose funding or tax benefits have standing to challenge line-item veto power, which was subsequently found unconstitutional as a violation of the federal legislative process.

(Choice A) The Eleventh Amendment generally prohibits suits in federal court against state governments—not federal officials (as seen here).

(Choice C) The political-question doctrine prevents federal courts from adjudicating issues that (1) are reserved to the executive or legislative branch or (2) lack judicially manageable standards for resolution. But since federal courts regularly determine the constitutionality of federal laws, this doctrine does not apply here.

(Choice D) The U.S. Supreme Court has exclusive jurisdiction over suits between states (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A legislator has standing to challenge the constitutionality of government action when that action causes the legislator personal and concrete harm—not institutional, abstract harm shared equally by all legislators in that respective body.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case-or-controversy requirement).
  • Raines v. Byrd, 521 U.S. 811, 829–30 (1997) (holding that members of Congress lack standing when the challenged government action causes an institutional and abstract harm instead of personal and concrete harm).
  • 32 Am. Jur. 2d Constitutional Law § 153 (2020) (explaining legislator standing requirements).
questions.zh-question:
为减少联邦赤字，国会通过并由总统签署成为法律的一项法规授予总统单项否决权。依据该权力，总统有权取消已经立法生效的特定支出和税收优惠措施。

几位投票反对该立法的国会议员已在联邦地区法院对相关联邦官员提起诉讼。这些国会议员主张该法规违宪，因为它违反了联邦立法程序的要求。联邦官员请求驳回此诉讼。

以下哪一项是法院驳回此诉讼的最恰当依据？

zh-choices.A: 第十一修正案禁止在联邦法院进行此类诉讼。
zh-choices.B: 国会议员不具有诉讼资格。
zh-choices.C: 该诉讼提出了一个不可由法院裁判的政治问题。
zh-choices.D: 美国最高法院对此诉讼拥有专属管辖权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法：司法审查与诉讼资格
正确答案：B 国会议员不具有诉讼资格 (Lack of Standing)。
⚖️ 核心法律原则

本题考察的是联邦法院管辖权中的核心门槛：诉讼资格 (Article III Standing)，特别是立法者的诉讼资格 (Legislator Standing)。

一般规则 (General Rule)

要拥有联邦法院的诉讼资格，原告必须证明：

  1. 事实上的损害 (Injury-in-fact)：具体的、特定的、实际发生的损害。
  2. 因果关系 (Causation)。
  3. 可补救性 (Redressability)。
立法者的特殊规则

国会议员通常没有资格挑战联邦法规的合宪性，除非他们遭受了个人的 (personal) 和 具体的 (concrete) 损害。

  • ❌ 制度性损害 (Institutional Injury)：如果损害仅仅是削弱了国会的整体权力（例如总统获得了过多权力），或者是所有议员共同分担的抽象政治损害，则不构成诉讼资格。
  • ✅ 选票无效 (Vote Nullification)：只有在极少数情况下（如议员的特定投票被非法剥夺效力），才可能具有诉讼资格。
📚 经典判例：Raines v. Byrd (1997)
本题的事实模式几乎直接取自该案。最高法院裁定，投票反对《单项否决权法案》(Line Item Veto Act) 的国会议员缺乏诉讼资格。法院认为，他们的损害是抽象的、制度性的（立法权力的稀释），而不是个人的具体损害。
🔍 案情应用

在本题中：

  • 原告是投票反对该法案的国会议员。
  • 他们主张该法案违宪，但这是一种政治上的损失。
  • 他们的投票已经被计算在内（只是输了），并没有被剥夺投票权。
  • 他们可以通过立法程序（如废除该法案）来寻求救济。

因此，他们遭受的是“制度性损害”，不足以确立 Article III 下的诉讼资格。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A (第十一修正案) 错误：
第十一修正案 (11th Amendment) 禁止公民在联邦法院起诉州政府 (States)。本案被告是联邦官员，因此不适用。
选项 C (政治问题) 错误：
虽然这涉及权力分立，但法院首先会检查诉讼资格 (Standing)。如果原告连门槛都进不去，法院不需要讨论这是否是政治问题 (Political Question)。此外，解释法规是否违宪通常是法院的职责，并非纯粹的政治问题。
选项 D (最高法院专属管辖) 错误：
最高法院的专属管辖权 (Exclusive Jurisdiction) 主要涉及州与州之间的诉讼。本案显然不属于此类。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

看到国会议员 (Members of Congress) 作为原告起诉联邦法律违宪时，请立即警惕 Standing (诉讼资格) 问题。

口诀：议员输了投票不开心，法院大门对他关（No Standing）。只有具体的私人利益受损（如工资被扣）或投票权被完全剥夺，才可能有资格。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state constitution provides that in every criminal trial "the accused shall have the right to confront all witnesses against him face to face." A defendant was convicted in state court of child abuse based on testimony from a six-year-old child. The child testified while she was seated behind one-way glass, which allowed the defendant to see the child but did not allow the child to see the defendant. The defendant appealed his conviction to the state's highest court, claiming that the inability of the child to see the defendant while she testified violated both the United States Constitution and the state constitution. Without addressing the federal constitutional issue, the state's highest court reversed the defendant's conviction and ordered a new trial. The court held that "the constitution of this state is clear, and it requires that while testifying in a criminal trial, a witness must be able to see the defendant." The state petitioned the United States Supreme Court for a writ of certiorari.
On which ground should the United States Supreme Court DENY the state's petition?

choices.A: A state may not seek appellate review in the United States Supreme Court of the reversal of a criminal conviction by its highest court.
choices.B: The decision of the state's highest court requires a new trial, and therefore it is not a final judgment.
choices.C: The decision of the state's highest court was based on an adequate and independent state ground.
choices.D: The Sixth Amendment to the United States Constitution does not require that a witness against a criminal defendant be able to see the defendant while the witness testifies.

questions.explanation:
The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has discretion to review a highest state court judgment that turns on federal law. But SCOTUS must decline to review a state court judgment based on state grounds that are:

  • adequate – the state grounds fully resolve the matter such that the application of federal law would not affect the outcome of the case and
  • independent – it is clear from the opinion that the state court did not rely on federal law in reaching its conclusion.

Here, the defendant appealed his conviction to the state's highest court, claiming violations of both the U.S. Constitution and the state constitution. Without addressing the federal constitutional issue, the court reversed his conviction on the ground that the state constitution clearly requires that a witness be able to see a criminal defendant while testifying. Since the court's decision was based on an adequate and independent state ground, SCOTUS should deny the state's petition for a writ of certiorari (ie, request for appellate review).

(Choice A) A state may seek appellate review in the Supreme Court of the reversal of a criminal conviction by the state's highest court. But SCOTUS must decline to review the reversal if it rests on adequate and independent state grounds.

(Choice B) Although the decision of the state's highest court requires a new trial, it is a final judgment since it fully resolves the confrontation issue—ie, whether witnesses must be able to see criminal defendants while testifying—and that issue will not arise on retrial.

(Choice D) A criminal defendant's Sixth Amendment right to confront adverse witnesses does not require that a witness be able to see the defendant while testifying. But here, SCOTUS would not reach the merits of the defendant's Sixth Amendment claim since the decision of the state's highest court was based entirely on state law.

📌 Educational Objective

The U.S. Supreme Court cannot review a state court judgment based on state-law grounds that are adequate (ie, the state grounds fully resolve the matter) AND independent (ie, the state court did not rely on federal law).

📚 References
  • Michigan v. Long, 463 U.S. 1032, 1041 (1983) (holding that a state supreme court judgment rests on adequate and independent state-law grounds if the state court makes a plain statement to that effect).
  • 4 Am. Jur. 2d Appellate Review § 44 (2019) (explaining the plain statement rule).
questions.zh-question:
某州宪法规定，在每起刑事审判中，“被告应有权与所有对他不利的证人当面对质。”一名被告因虐待儿童罪在州法院被定罪，定罪依据是一名六岁儿童的证词。该儿童在作证时坐在一块单向玻璃后面，这使得被告能看到该儿童，但该儿童无法看到被告。被告向该州的最高法院就其定罪提起上诉，声称该儿童在作证时无法看到被告，这既违反了 United States Constitution，也违反了州宪法。州最高法院未处理联邦宪法问题，而是撤销了被告的有罪判决，并下令进行新的审判。该法院裁定，“本州宪法规定明确，要求在刑事审判中作证时，证人必须能够看到被告。”该州向 United States Supreme Court 申请调卷令（writ of certiorari）。

United States Supreme Court 应基于何种理由驳回该州的申请？

zh-choices.A: 对于州最高法院撤销刑事定罪的判决，州政府不得向 United States Supreme Court 寻求上诉复审。
zh-choices.B: 州最高法院的判决要求进行新的审判，因此它不是一项终审判决。
zh-choices.C: 州最高法院的判决基于充分且独立的州法律依据。
zh-choices.D: United States Constitution Sixth Amendment 不要求对刑事被告不利的证人在作证时必须能够看到被告。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

司法审查权与州法依据
核心原则：AISG

Adequate and Independent State Grounds (充分且独立的州法依据)

如果州最高法院的判决完全基于州法律（如州宪法），且该依据足以解决案件，不依赖于联邦法律，那么美国最高法院（SCOTUS）无权复审该案件。

本案逻辑链条分析
1
州法院的判决依据：
州最高法院明确指出，依据本州宪法 (State Constitution)，证人必须能看到被告。
2
忽略联邦法：
法院明确表示“未处理联邦宪法问题” (Without addressing the federal constitutional issue)。这意味着判决是独立 (Independent) 的。
3
结果的不可变性：
即使 SCOTUS 受理此案并裁定联邦宪法（第六修正案）允许使用单向玻璃，州法院仍会依据州宪法（提供比联邦更高的保护）维持原判（撤销定罪）。
4
结论：
州法依据是充分 (Adequate) 的，因为它足以决定案件结果。SCOTUS 若介入，只能提供无法改变结果的“咨询意见” (Advisory Opinion)，这是宪法禁止的。
✅ 正确答案：选项 C

理由：州最高法院的判决基于充分且独立的州法律依据 (Adequate and Independent State Ground)。

这是 SCOTUS 拒绝签发调卷令 (Writ of Certiorari) 的经典理由。只要州法院明确声明其判决仅依赖于州法，联邦最高法院就不会干预。

❌ 选项 A 错误：
州政府可以就刑事案件的逆转判决向 SCOTUS 上诉，前提是该判决涉及联邦问题且不是基于 AISG。
❌ 选项 B 错误：
虽然案件被发回重审，但这在司法审查的语境下被视为终审判决 (Final Judgment)，因为关于“对质权”的法律规则已经由该州最高法院最终确定了。
❌ 选项 D 错误：
虽然这是对联邦宪法第六修正案的正确陈述（联邦法确实不强制要求面对面可见），但 SCOTUS 根本不会审理实体问题，因为管辖权被 AISG 原则阻断了。
💡 MBE 技巧：
看到题目中出现“州最高法院依据州宪法”、“未讨论联邦问题”或“州法规定明确”等字眼时，优先考虑 AISG 原则。记住判例 Michigan v. Long 确立的“明确声明规则” (Plain Statement Rule)。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A nightclub owner applied for a required zoning permit to open a nude-dancing nightclub in the theater district of a city. An organization of influential city residents began an intensive lobbying effort to persuade the city council to deny the owner a permit to operate any type of nude-dancing facility at any time or in any place in the city.
The owner has sued the city in an appropriate federal court, seeking an injunction that would prohibit the city council from considering the organization's views, on the ground that if the organization is successful in its lobbying efforts, the owner's First and Fourteenth Amendment rights would be violated. The city has moved to dismiss the action.
Should the court dismiss the owner's action?

choices.A: No, because nude dancing is symbolic speech and is therefore protected by the First and Fourteenth Amendments.
choices.B: No, because the organization does not seek a reasonable time, place, and manner regulation of nude dancing, but instead seeks a total ban on the owner's opening any type of nude-dancing facility at any time or in any place in the city.
choices.C: Yes, because the action is not ripe.
choices.D: Yes, because the First and Fourteenth Amendments do not protect obscenity, and nude dancing is obscene.

questions.explanation:
Article III of the Constitution limits the jurisdiction of federal courts to actual cases or controversies. An actual case or controversy exists when a dispute between adverse parties is capable of judicial resolution—ie, ripe for adjudication. A suit is ripe when the plaintiff has suffered actual harm or an immediate threat thereof. But a suit based on potential future harm is unripe and should be dismissed.

Here, the nightclub owner applied for a permit to open a nude-dancing facility. An organization then lobbied the city council to deny the permit. In response, the owner sued in federal court to enjoin the city council from considering the organization's views. But the city council has not yet denied his permit request (no actual harm), nor is there any indication that it will do so soon (no immediate threat). And since the owner's action is not ripe, the court should grant the city's motion and dismiss the suit.

(Choices A & B) Nude dancing is symbolic speech that is protected by the First and Fourteenth Amendments. As a result, a total ban on nude dancing (ie, a content-based restriction) would be presumptively unconstitutional. In contrast, a reasonable time, place, and manner (ie, content-neutral) regulation would likely be valid. But the court will not consider the constitutionality of the potential regulation since the suit is unripe.

(Choice D) The First and Fourteenth Amendments do not protect certain forms of speech, including obscenity. But mere nudity (including nude dancing) is not obscene.

📌 Educational Objective

For a suit to be ripe for adjudication, the plaintiff must have suffered actual harm or an immediate threat thereof. Therefore, a claim based on potential future harm is unripe and will be dismissed.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case or controversy requirement).
  • Texas v. United States, 523 U.S. 296, 300 (1998) (explaining when a claim is unripe for adjudication).
questions.zh-question:
一位夜总会老板申请了必要的区域规划许可，欲在某市的剧院区开设一家裸体舞夜总会。一个由该市有影响力的居民组成的组织发起了一场密集的游说活动，试图说服市议会拒绝向该老板颁发任何类型、任何时间、任何地点的裸体舞设施的经营许可。

该老板已在相应的联邦法院对该市提起诉讼，寻求一项禁令，禁止市议会考虑该组织的观点，理由是如果该组织的游说活动成功，老板根据第一和第十四修正案所享有的权利将受到侵犯。该市已提出动议，要求驳回此诉讼。

法院是否应驳回该老板的诉讼？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为裸体舞是象征性言论，因此受到第一和第十四修正案的保护。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为该组织并非寻求对裸体舞进行合理的时间、地点和方式的规制，而是寻求全面禁止该老板在任何时间、任何地点开设任何类型的裸体舞设施。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为该诉讼尚未成熟。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为第一和第十四修正案不保护淫秽内容，而裸体舞是淫秽的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Justiciability
💡 核心考点：成熟度原则 (Ripeness)

本题考查的是联邦法院管辖权中的可诉性 (Justiciability) 问题，具体为成熟度 (Ripeness)。

根据美国宪法第三条 (Article III)，联邦法院只能审理实际存在的“案件或争议” (Cases or Controversies)，不能发布咨询性意见 (Advisory Opinions)。

✅ 正确答案分析 (选项 C)

法院应当驳回诉讼，因为案件尚未成熟 (Not Ripe)。

法律依据：
一个案件要达到“成熟”的标准，原告必须已经遭受了实际损害 (Actual Harm) 或面临迫在眉睫的威胁 (Immediate Threat)。如果损害是推测性的 (Speculative) 或取决于未来不确定的事件，则案件不成熟。

本案逻辑：

  • 现状：老板申请了许可，游说团体正在游说市议会拒绝。
  • 缺失环节：市议会尚未做出决定。他们可能会拒绝游说团体的建议，批准老板的许可。
  • 结论：在市议会正式拒绝许可之前，老板没有遭受实际的宪法权利侵害。法院不会介入去阻止立法者“听取意见”。
❌ 干扰项排除
选项 A & B 错误原因：程序优于实体

这两个选项都在讨论第一修正案 (First Amendment) 的实体问题（象征性言论、时间地点方式规制）。

虽然裸体舞确实属于受保护的象征性言论 (Symbolic Speech)，且全面禁止 (Total Ban) 通常违宪，但法院首先必须有管辖权。既然案件不成熟（程序性障碍），法院根本不会审理实体问题。

选项 D 错误原因：法律定义错误

虽然淫秽内容 (Obscenity) 不受保护，但根据最高法院判例（如 Miller v. California），单纯的裸体或非淫秽的裸体舞通常不被视为法律意义上的“淫秽”，而是受保护的表达形式。更重要的是，这也是在讨论实体问题，而非管辖权问题。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

当题目中出现以下情况时，优先考虑成熟度 (Ripeness) 问题：

  1. 政府机构尚未通过法律或做出最终决定。
  2. 原告试图在法律生效前或决定做出前寻求禁令 (Injunction) 或宣告性判决 (Declaratory Judgment)。
  3. 题目问“法院是否应该驳回”或“法院最可能的裁决是什么”。

记住口诀：No Harm, No Foul (Yet). 没有实际损害或紧迫威胁，联邦法院不开门。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute provides states with funds for child welfare programs, subject to the condition that such programs be administered in accordance with federal standards.
The United States sued a state in federal court for injunctive relief, arguing that the state's child welfare programs, which were funded in part by federal funds disbursed under this statute, failed to comply with federal standards. The state has moved to dismiss the action.
Is the court likely to dismiss the action?

choices.A: No, because Congress can place any condition on the receipt of federal funds.
choices.B: No, because the Eleventh Amendment does not bar actions brought by the United States.
choices.C: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment bars actions against a state in federal court.
choices.D: Yes, because the protection of child welfare is reserved to the states.

questions.explanation:
Eleventh Amendment
(state immunity from suit in federal court)
Immunity
  • Suit brought by private party or foreign government
  • Suit against state official violating state law
  • Exceptions:
    • State consents to suit
    • Immunity removed by 13th, 14th, or 15th Amendment
    • State official sued for injunctive or declaratory relief for alleged constitutional violation
    • Damages to be paid by state officer personally (not state treasury)
    • State official sued for prospective (not retroactive) damages to be paid by state treasury
No
immunity
  • Suit brought by United States or other state
  • Suit against local government (eg, counties, municipalities)
  • Bankruptcy proceedings
  • Eminent domain proceedings
  • Suits permitted by Congress pursuant to its powers over war & armed forces

The Eleventh Amendment prohibits private parties and foreign governments from suing a state in federal court without the state's consent.* However, this amendment does not bar actions brought by the United States or another state. And since the United States sued the state here for injunctive relief, the Eleventh Amendment does not apply. As a result, the federal court likely will not dismiss this action (Choice C).

*Additionally, the doctrine of sovereign immunity bars private federal-law actions against a state sued in the courts of that state or any other state without the state's consent.

(Choice A) Congress may place certain conditions on the receipt of federal funds. Such conditions are valid if they (1) are unambiguous, (2) relate to the funded program's purpose, and (3) are not unduly coercive. Therefore, the federal court likely will retain this suit and determine if this funding condition satisfies these requirements.

(Choice D) Under the Tenth Amendment, all powers not expressly granted to the federal government by the Constitution are reserved to the states—eg, the power over child welfare. But the federal government can use its taxing and spending power to encourage states to adopt certain policies by placing conditions on the receipt of federal funds—eg, requiring state-recipients to comply with federal standards (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The Eleventh Amendment bars private parties and foreign governments from suing a state in federal court without the state's consent. But it does not bar suits brought by the United States or another state.

📚 References
  • Principality of Monaco v. Mississippi, 292 U.S. 313, 329 (1934) (stating that the Eleventh Amendment does not bar a suit by the United States against a state in federal court).
  • 32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 91 (2019) (explaining that the United States may sue a state in federal court without the state's consent).
questions.zh-question:
一项联邦法规为各州提供儿童福利项目资金，但条件是此类项目必须按照联邦标准进行管理。

美国政府在联邦法院对一个州提起诉讼，请求禁令救济，理由是该州的儿童福利项目（部分资金来自该法规拨付的联邦资金）未能遵守联邦标准。该州已动议驳回此诉讼。

法院是否可能驳回此诉讼？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为国会可以为联邦资金的接收附加任何条件。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为《第十一修正案》不禁止由美国政府提起的诉讼。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为《第十一修正案》禁止在联邦法院对州提起诉讼。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为保护儿童福利是保留给各州的权力。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law / Federal Jurisdiction
正确答案：B
核心考点：第十一修正案
第十一修正案 (Eleventh Amendment) 确立了各州在联邦法院的主权豁免权 (Sovereign Immunity)。

这意味着，通常情况下，私人当事方（Private Parties）或外国政府不能在联邦法院起诉一个州。
法律规则详解

虽然第十一修正案限制了针对州的诉讼，但这一豁免权并非绝对。以下是主要的例外情况：

  • 联邦政府提起的诉讼： 美国联邦政府（United States）可以在联邦法院起诉任何一个州，无需该州同意。
  • 州与州之间的诉讼： 一个州可以起诉另一个州。
  • 州表示同意（Waiver）： 州明确放弃豁免权。
  • 国会废除（Abrogation）： 国会根据第十四修正案第5款明确废除州的豁免权。
本题案情分析

本题的关键在于识别原告（Plaintiff）和被告（Defendant）的身份：

  • 原告： 美国政府 (The United States)
  • 被告： 某州 (A State)

根据上述法律规则，第十一修正案并不禁止联邦政府起诉州政府。无论诉讼请求是金钱赔偿还是禁令救济（Injunctive Relief），只要原告是美国联邦政府，州就没有主权豁免权。

因此，法院不会因为第十一修正案而驳回此案。

干扰项辨析
选项 A 错误
虽然国会可以通过支出权 (Spending Power) 附加条件，但该选项称国会可以附加“任何条件” (any condition) 是错误的。条件必须与项目相关、明确且不具有过度胁迫性。更重要的是，这涉及案件的实体问题，而题目问的是程序性的驳回动议。
选项 C 错误
这是对第十一修正案的一般性描述，但忽略了本案的关键例外：原告是美国政府。
选项 D 错误
虽然儿童福利通常属于州的保留权力 (Reserved Powers)，但根据 South Dakota v. Dole，联邦政府可以通过财政拨款（Spending Power）来诱导州遵守联邦标准，这并不违反第十修正案。
💡 MBE 解题技巧 在处理涉及第十一修正案 (11th Amendment) 的题目时，第一步永远是检查“谁在起诉谁”：

如果是 US v. State 或 State v. State，直接排除“主权豁免”选项。豁免权主要针对的是私人 (Private Citizens) 起诉州的情况。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute provides funds to private organizations that develop online learning materials for schools. A provision of the statute requires organizations that receive such funds to provide their educational materials to private, religious schools for use in their curriculum on the same terms that the organizations provide to public schools.
A taxpayer brought a suit in federal court to challenge the federal statutory provision as violating the establishment clause of the First Amendment. The taxpayer does not work in the education industry, nor does he have any children.
Does the taxpayer have standing to challenge the provision?

choices.A: No, because the private organizations receiving the federal funds are not state actors.
choices.B: No, because the provision did not cause the taxpayer to suffer a concrete and particularized injury.
choices.C: Yes, because taxpayers have the right to challenge how Congress spends federal funds.
choices.D: Yes, because the taxpayer's challenge is based on the establishment clause.

questions.explanation:
Article III standing (suing on one's own behalf)
General rule Plaintiff must prove:
  • injury-in-fact – concrete & particularized harm (actual or imminent)
  • causation – harm traceable to defendant's conduct AND
  • redressability – favorable judicial decision can remedy harm
Citizen No standing as mere citizen
Legislator Must prove personal stake in dispute & concrete injury to challenge constitutionality of government action
Taxpayer Standing to challenge taxes owed—but not government spending unless:
  • challenging legislation enacted under taxing & spending power AND
  • legislation exceeds limits imposed by establishment clause

A federal court will not hear a case unless the plaintiff has standing—i.e., a personal stake in the outcome of the case. To have standing, the plaintiff must assert an injury-in-fact that is concrete and particularized—a generalized grievance shared by many or all citizens is insufficient. Therefore, taxpayers lack standing to challenge the way the government spends tax dollars unless the taxpayer:

  • challenges legislation enacted under Congress's or a state's taxing and spending power and
  • alleges a violation of a specific constitutional limitation on this power—to date, the only limitation that the U.S. Supreme Court has found is the First Amendment establishment clause.

Here, the taxpayer is challenging a federal statute that provides funds to private organizations to develop online learning materials for schools (exercise of congressional spending power). He is specifically challenging the statutory provision requiring such organizations to provide materials to private, religious schools as a violation of the First Amendment establishment clause (specific constitutional limitation). The taxpayer therefore has standing to challenge this provision.

(Choice A) With the exception of the Thirteenth Amendment, the Constitution applies to government (i.e., state) action. Private action is considered government action only if the state-action doctrine applies. But here, the taxpayer is challenging a federal law, so there is no need to determine whether the private organizations are engaging in state action.

(Choice B) The statutory provision did not cause the taxpayer to suffer a concrete and particularized injury since he does not work in the education industry and does not have children who may be affected by the provision. However, as a taxpayer, he has standing to challenge the provision as violative of the establishment clause.

(Choice C) Taxpayers have the right to challenge how Congress spends federal funds only when the challenge alleges a violation of a specific constitutional limitation on Congress's taxing and spending power (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A plaintiff-taxpayer has standing when his/her suit (1) challenges legislation enacted under Congress's taxing and spending power and (2) alleges a violation of a specific constitutional limitation on that power (i.e., the establishment clause).

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (defining the case-or-controversy requirement).
  • Flast v. Cohen, 392 U.S. 83, 102–04 (1968) (establishing the narrow exception to the rule against taxpayer standing).

主题：宪法 — 司法审查

该纳税人是否有 standing 来质疑该条款？

zh-choices.B: 否，因为该条款并未导致纳税人遭受 concrete and particularized injury。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为纳税人有权质疑国会如何使用联邦资金。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法：司法审查

正确答案: D

纳税人有权挑战国会根据税收和支出权力制定的立法，如果该挑战是基于对特定宪法限制（如第一修正案的政教分离条款）的违反。

核心法律规则

诉讼资格 (Standing)

联邦法院只有在原告具有诉讼资格 (standing) 时才会审理案件，即原告必须在案件结果中拥有个人利害关系。要具备诉讼资格，原告必须主张存在一项事实上的伤害 (injury-in-fact)，该伤害是具体且特定化的，而非由许多或所有公民共享的普遍性不满。因此，纳税人通常缺乏挑战政府支出方式的诉讼资格，除非满足以下狭义例外：

  • 挑战的立法是根据国会的税收和支出权力 (taxing and spending power) 制定的；并且
  • 指控该立法违反了对国会该权力施加的特定宪法限制 (specific constitutional limitation)。迄今为止，唯一的此类限制是第一修正案的政教分离条款 (Establishment Clause)。

此例外被称为 Flast v. Cohen 规则。

概念对比：不同主体的诉讼资格

主体 诉讼资格要求
一般规则 原告必须证明：
  • 事实上的伤害 (injury-in-fact) – 具体且特定化的伤害（实际或迫在眉睫）
  • 因果关系 (causation) – 伤害可追溯至被告的行为 AND
  • 可救济性 (redressability) – 有利的司法裁决可以补救伤害
普通公民 作为普通公民无诉讼资格。
立法者 必须证明在争议中存在个人利害关系和具体伤害，才能挑战政府行为的合宪性。
纳税人 挑战所欠税款有诉讼资格，但挑战政府支出通常没有，除非：
  • 挑战的立法是根据国会的税收和支出权力制定的 AND
  • 挑战的立法超出了政教分离条款所施加的限制。

案件事实与法律适用

本案中，纳税人挑战一项联邦法规，该法规向私人组织提供资金，用于开发学校在线学习材料（行使国会支出权力）。该法规的一项条款要求接受资金的组织向私人宗教学校提供教育材料，这被指控违反了第一修正案的政教分离条款 (Establishment Clause)（一项具体的宪法限制）。

根据 Flast v. Cohen 规则，纳税人对联邦支出立法的挑战满足了纳税人诉讼资格的两个条件：

  1. 该法规是根据国会的税收和支出权力 (taxing and spending power) 制定的。
  2. 该挑战指控该法规违反了第一修正案的政教分离条款 (Establishment Clause)，这是对国会支出权力的一项特定宪法限制。

因此，该纳税人具有挑战该条款的诉讼资格。

纳税人诉讼资格判断流程图

纳税人挑战政府行为
↓
涉及国会税收与支出权力？
否 ↓
无诉讼资格
是 ↓
指控违反特定宪法限制？
(如政教分离条款)
否 ↓
无诉讼资格
是 ↓
有诉讼资格

MBE 考点陷阱提示

陷阱： 混淆普通公民诉讼资格与纳税人诉讼资格的狭义例外。

普通公民通常没有诉讼资格挑战政府行为，除非他们遭受了具体且特定化的伤害。纳税人也通常没有诉讼资格挑战政府支出，因为这被认为是普遍性不满。然而，Flast v. Cohen 规则为纳税人提供了一个非常狭窄的例外，专门针对挑战国会根据其税收和支出权力制定的立法，且该挑战基于第一修正案的政教分离条款 (Establishment Clause)。

注意： Flast 例外不适用于挑战行政行为，也不适用于挑战其他宪法条款的违反（如商业条款）。它严格限于政教分离条款和国会支出。

正确答案与干扰项排除

A. 错误。 本案中，纳税人挑战的是一项联邦法规，而非私人组织的行动。因此，国家行为原则 (state-action doctrine) 在此不适用，因为挑战对象本身就是政府行为。

B. 错误。 尽管通常情况下，纳税人必须遭受具体且特定化的伤害才能获得诉讼资格，但 Flast v. Cohen 规则为挑战国会支出违反政教分离条款的情况提供了一个狭义例外。在这种特定情况下，纳税人无需证明个人具体伤害即可获得诉讼资格。

C. 错误。 这种说法过于宽泛。纳税人通常没有普遍的权利挑战国会如何花费联邦资金，因为这被视为普遍性不满。只有当挑战符合 Flast v. Cohen 规则的严格条件时（即涉及国会税收和支出权力，并指控违反政教分离条款），纳税人才具有诉讼资格。因此，选项 D 更准确地描述了纳税人诉讼资格的条件。

D. 正确。 根据 Flast v. Cohen 规则，纳税人有诉讼资格挑战国会根据其税收和支出权力制定的立法，如果该挑战是基于对第一修正案政教分离条款 (Establishment Clause) 的违反。本案中，纳税人正是挑战一项联邦支出法规违反了政教分离条款，因此符合该例外条件。

备考小贴士

记住纳税人诉讼资格是一个非常狭窄的例外。它仅适用于挑战国会根据其税收和支出权力制定的立法，且该挑战必须基于第一修正案的政教分离条款 (Establishment Clause)。对于其他类型的政府支出或宪法条款的挑战，纳税人通常不具备诉讼资格。
