questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress recently enacted a statute imposing severe criminal penalties on anyone engaged in trading in the stock market who, in the course of that trading, takes "unfair advantage" of other investors who are also trading in the stock market. The statute does not define the term "unfair advantage." There have been no prosecutions under this new statute.
The members of an association of law school professors that is dedicated to increasing the clarity of the language used in criminal statutes believe that this statute is unconstitutionally vague. Neither the association nor any of its members is currently engaged in, or intends in the future to engage in, trading in the stock market.
The association and its members bring suit against the Attorney General of the United States in a federal district court, seeking an injunction against the enforcement of this statute on the ground that it is unconstitutional.
May the federal court determine the merits of this suit?

choices.A: No, because a suit for an injunction against enforcement of a criminal statute may not be brought in federal court at any time prior to a bona fide effort to enforce that statute.
choices.B: No, because the plaintiffs do not have an interest in invalidating this statute that is adequate to ensure that the suit presents an Article III controversy.
choices.C: Yes, because the plaintiffs seek real relief of a conclusive nature—an injunction against enforcement of this statute.
choices.D: Yes, because the suit involves a dispute over the constitutionality of a federal statute.

questions.explanation:
Article III only allows federal courts to determine the merits of actual cases or controversies. The doctrine of standing ensures that this requirement is met by requiring the plaintiff to show that he/she has a personal stake in the outcome of the case. This exists when the plaintiff has suffered an injury-in-fact—ie, concrete and particularized harm that is actual or imminent—that was caused by the challenged conduct and is redressable by a favorable decision.

Here, the association and its members sued in federal court to challenge the constitutionality of the stock market statute. But the statute has not caused these plaintiffs an injury-in-fact because neither is currently engaged in, or intends to engage in, stock market trading (no actual or imminent harm). This means that the plaintiffs do not have an interest in invalidating the statute that would satisfy Article III's case-or-controversy requirement. As a result, the court cannot determine the merits of their suit.

(Choice A) Even if a criminal statute has not been enforced, a suit for an injunction to prevent such enforcement may be brought in federal court if the plaintiff shows that the statute poses an immediate threat of harm (not seen here).

(Choice C) The injunction would provide real and conclusive relief. But the federal court does not have the power to issue an injunction in a suit that does not meet the case-or-controversy requirement (as seen here).

(Choice D) Federal courts have subject-matter jurisdiction over suits involving the constitutionality of federal statutes. But the court cannot hear the merits of such a suit when, as here, the plaintiffs lack standing to assert their constitutional challenge.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the doctrine of standing, an injury-in-fact exists when the plaintiff has suffered concrete and particularized harm that is actual or imminent.

📚 References
  • Lujan v. Defs. of Wildlife, 504 U.S. 555, 560–61 (1992) (holding that standing requires proof of an injury-in-fact, causation, and redressability).
questions.zh-question:
国会最近颁布了一项法规，对任何在股票市场交易中，利用其他同样在进行股票交易的投资者的“不公平优势”的人，处以严厉的刑事处罚。该法规未定义“不公平优势”这一术语。目前尚无根据此新法规提起的诉讼。

一个致力于提高刑事法语言清晰度的法学院教授协会的成员们认为，该法规因含糊不清而违宪。该协会及其任何成员目前没有，也无意在将来从事股票市场交易。

该协会及其成员向美国联邦地区法院对美国司法部长提起诉讼，以该法规违宪为由，请求法院颁布禁止执行该法规的禁令。

联邦法院能否就此案的实体问题作出裁决？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为在善意执行某刑事法规之前，任何时候都不得向联邦法院提起旨在禁止执行该法规的禁令之诉。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为原告在宣告该法规无效一事上不具有充分的利益，以确保该诉讼构成 Article III 所规定的争议。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为原告寻求的是具有确定性的实际救济——一项禁止执行该法规的禁令。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为该诉讼涉及一项关于联邦法规合宪性的争议。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法：司法审查与诉讼资格
⚖️ 核心考点：诉讼资格 (Standing)

根据美国宪法第三条 (Article III)，联邦法院只能审理真实的“案件或争议” (Cases or Controversies)。

原告必须证明以下三要素才能拥有 Standing：
  1. 事实上的损害 (Injury-in-fact)： 损害必须是具体且特定的 (concrete and particularized)，且是实际发生或迫在眉睫的 (actual or imminent)。
  2. 因果关系 (Causation)： 损害与被告的行为之间有因果联系。
  3. 可救济性 (Redressability)： 法院的有利判决能够补救该损害。

本题考察的重点在于第一点：是否存在事实上的损害？

🔍 案情分析

事实：法学院教授协会起诉要求禁止执行一项关于股票交易的刑事法规。理由是该法规模糊不清。

关键点：

❌ 无交易行为： 协会及其成员目前没有，也无意将来从事股票交易。
❌ 无被起诉风险： 既然不交易，他们就不可能违反该法，也不面临被起诉的“迫在眉睫的威胁” (Imminent threat of prosecution)。
❌ 仅有学术兴趣： 他们唯一的诉求是“提高法律清晰度”。这属于普遍的不满 (Generalized Grievance)，而非个人化的损害。

结论： 原告缺乏 Article III 要求的“个人利害关系” (Personal Stake)，因此法院无权审理。

✅ 正确答案：B

理由： 原告缺乏足以确保该诉讼构成 Article III 争议的利益。

因为原告不从事股票交易，该法规不会对他们造成任何实际的或迫在眉睫的伤害。仅仅因为关心法律的清晰度而提起诉讼，不足以建立联邦法院的管辖权。

❌ 错误选项辨析
选项 A (关于执行前审查)：
错误。虽然通常需要等待执法，但如果法规构成了“直接且即刻的威胁”，原告是可以提起执行前审查 (Pre-enforcement review) 的。本题错误不在于时间点，而在于原告根本没有受到威胁。
选项 C (关于救济性质)：
错误。虽然禁令 (Injunction) 确实是有效的救济手段，但如果原告一开始就没有 Standing，法院根本无权颁布禁令。救济手段不能反推管辖权。
选项 D (关于属事管辖权)：
错误。虽然联邦法院确实有权审理关于联邦法律合宪性的案件（属事管辖权 Subject Matter Jurisdiction），但这并不免除原告必须拥有 Standing 的要求。这是两个独立的门槛。
💡 备考小贴士

在做 Constitutional Law 的题目时，如果看到原告是纳税人 (Taxpayer)、关注社会的公民 (Concerned Citizen) 或学术团体，请立即警惕 Standing 问题。

除非有特定的例外（如 Establishment Clause 挑战），否则单纯的“意识形态兴趣”或“希望政府守法”的愿望，永远不足以构成 Standing。

MBE 模拟题解析 | 宪法学

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute requires the National Bureau of Standards to establish minimum quality standards for all beer sold in the United States. The statute also provides that public hearings must precede adoption of the standards, and that once they are adopted, the standards will be subject to judicial review. While the proposed standards have not yet been announced, several Bureau officials have publicly expressed opinions indicating a belief that pasteurized beer is safer than unpasteurized beer. However, these officials have not stated whether they intend to include a pasteurization requirement in the standards.
A brewery that produces unpasteurized beer is concerned that, after the appropriate proceedings, the Bureau may adopt quality standards that will prohibit the sale of unpasteurized beer. The brewery has sued in federal district court to enjoin the Bureau from adopting standards that would prohibit the sale of unpasteurized beer.
How should the district court proceed with the suit?

choices.A: Determine whether the Bureau could reasonably believe that pasteurization is the safest process by which to brew beer and, if so, refuse to issue the injunction against the Bureau.
choices.B: Determine whether the process used by the brewery is as safe as pasteurization and, if so, issue the injunction against the Bureau.
choices.C: Refuse to adjudicate the merits of the suit and dismiss it, because it does not involve a justiciable case or controversy.
choices.D: Refuse to adjudicate the merits of the suit at this time and stay the action until the Bureau has actually issued beer-quality standards.

questions.explanation:
Justiciability
(suitability for judicial resolution)
Case or controversy Prohibits advisory opinions under three doctrines:
  • Standing – plaintiff must allege injury-in-fact caused by challenged action & redressable by remedy sought
  • Ripeness – claim must present actual controversy involving past injury or present threat of injury
  • Mootness – claim must be unresolved
Adequate & independent state grounds SCOTUS cannot review final state court judgment that rests on adequate & independent state grounds
Political question Court cannot hear case if issue presented:
  • is reserved for executive/legislative branches or
  • lacks judicially manageable standards for resolution
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States.

A federal court should not proceed with a suit unless it is justiciable—ie, appropriate for judicial resolution—based on the following Article III requirements: (1) case or controversy, (2) no adequate and independent state grounds, and (3) no political questions. The case-or-controversy requirement is met if the plaintiff has standing—ie, suffered an injury-in-fact that was caused by the defendant and is redressable by the court. An injury-in-fact exists if the plaintiff alleges actual, or an immediate threat of, harm. Therefore, a court should dismiss a suit that is:

  • unripe – the suit is based on the mere potential for, or future threat of, harm or
  • moot – the suit no longer presents a live (ie, actual) controversy for the court to resolve.

Here, the brewery filed suit in federal district court to enjoin the Bureau from adopting standards that would prohibit the brewery from selling unpasteurized beer. But this suit does not involve a justiciable case or controversy because the Bureau has not adopted such standards (no actual harm) and public hearings that must precede the adoption have yet to occur (no imminent harm). Therefore, the court should refuse to adjudicate the merits of this unripe suit and dismiss it.

(Choices A & B) Since this suit is not justiciable, the court cannot consider its merits—eg, whether (1) the Bureau could reasonably believe that pasteurization is the safest process or (2) the brewery's process is as safe as pasteurization.

(Choice D) A federal court can stay (ie, suspend) a suit to (1) force a party to comply with a court order or (2) protect a party's rights. However, a federal court must dismiss a suit when, as here, it does not present a justiciable case or controversy.

📌 Educational Objective

Article III limits the jurisdiction of federal courts to justiciable cases or controversies. This requires proof that the plaintiff has suffered an injury-in-fact—ie, an actual, or immediate threat of, harm. Therefore, a federal court must dismiss a suit involving future or resolved harm.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case or controversy requirement).
  • Texas v. United States, 523 U.S. 296, 300 (1998) (explaining when a claim is unripe for adjudication).
questions.zh-question:
一项联邦法规要求国家标准局（National Bureau of Standards）为在美国销售的所有啤酒制定最低质量标准。该法规还规定，在通过这些标准之前必须举行公开听证会，并且一旦通过，这些标准将接受司法审查。尽管拟议的标准尚未公布，但该局的几名官员已公开发表意见，表示他们相信巴氏杀菌啤酒比未经巴氏杀菌的啤酒更安全。然而，这些官员并未说明他们是否打算在标准中加入巴氏杀菌的要求。

一家生产未经巴氏杀菌啤酒的啤酒厂担心，在经过适当程序后，该局可能会通过禁止销售未经巴氏杀菌啤酒的质量标准。该啤酒厂已向联邦地区法院提起诉讼，请求法院发布禁令，禁止该局通过会禁止销售未经巴氏杀菌啤酒的标准。

地区法院应如何处理此案？

zh-choices.A: 裁定该局是否可以合理地认为巴氏杀菌是酿造啤酒最安全的流程，如果可以，则拒绝向该局发出禁令。
zh-choices.B: 裁定该啤酒厂使用的流程是否与巴氏杀菌同样安全，如果是，则向该局发出禁令。
zh-choices.C: 拒绝就案件的实体问题进行裁决并驳回诉讼，因为该案不涉及可诉的案件或争议。
zh-choices.D: 在此时拒绝就案件的实体问题进行裁决，并中止诉讼程序，直到该局实际发布了啤酒质量标准。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法学：司法审查与可诉性
正确答案：C 法院应拒绝就案件实体问题进行裁决并驳回诉讼，因为该案尚未成熟（Unripe），不构成可诉的“案件或争议”。
核心考点：成熟性 (Ripeness)

美国宪法第三条（Article III）限制联邦法院只能审理实际的“案件或争议” (Cases or Controversies)。法院禁止发布咨询意见 (Advisory Opinions)。

成熟性原则 (Ripeness Doctrine) 要求：

  • 原告所受的伤害必须是实际发生的或迫在眉睫的 (Imminent)。
  • 如果伤害取决于未来的、不确定的事件（可能发生也可能不发生），则案件“不成熟”，法院无管辖权。
本案逻辑分析

在本题中，法院必须驳回诉讼，理由如下：

  1. 程序尚未完成：法规明确规定，在通过标准前必须举行“公开听证会”。这一步骤尚未发生。
  2. 结果不确定：虽然官员发表了个人意见，但官方并没有正式提出或通过任何禁止非巴氏杀菌啤酒的标准。行政机构完全可能在听证会后改变主意。
  3. 缺乏实际伤害：啤酒厂目前面临的只是“猜测性”的伤害。在标准正式发布之前，没有任何法律禁止他们销售啤酒。

因此，现在进行司法审查为时过早（Premature），属于请求法院对假设性情况发表意见。

为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A & B (错误)：涉及实体问题 (Merits)
这两个选项都建议法院去审查“哪个流程更安全”。这是案件的实体 (Merits)。如果法院连管辖权（Jurisdiction）都没有（因为案件不可诉），它就绝对不能触及实体问题。
选项 D (错误)：中止 (Stay) vs. 驳回 (Dismiss)
如果一个案件缺乏宪法规定的“案件或争议”要件，联邦法院没有权力保留该案件。它必须直接驳回 (Dismiss)，而不是仅仅中止程序等待结果。中止通常用于案件本身可诉，但需要等待其他程序结果的情况。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

当你在宪法题中看到原告试图阻止政府“计划做”或“正在考虑做”某事，但政府还没有正式行动（颁布法规、通过法律）时：

  • 首先检查成熟性 (Ripeness)。
  • 如果行政程序（如听证会、公众评论期）还没走完，或者法律还没生效，通常选“Dismiss / Not Justiciable”。
  • 记住口诀：No Harm, No Foul (没有实际伤害，就没有诉讼)。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The federal parole commission denied a federal prisoner's request for parole based on the commission's parole guidelines. The prisoner subsequently filed a class action against the commission in federal court, challenging the facial validity of the commission's parole guidelines on the basis that the guidelines violate federal law. After the court certified the class action, the prisoner was released from prison. The commission has moved to dismiss the case.
Should the court grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because an actual case or controversy exists for the court to decide.
choices.B: No, because the prisoner's suit is not ripe for decision.
choices.C: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits this type of action in federal court.
choices.D: Yes, because the prisoner's claim has become moot.

questions.explanation:
Ripeness v. Mootness
Ripe
(too soon) 		Action will not be heard until plaintiff has experienced actual injury or imminent threat thereof
Moot
(too late) 		Action will be dismissed if further proceedings would have no effect unless:
  • plaintiff's harm is capable of repetition yet evading review (eg, pregnancy)
  • defendant voluntarily stops action but can resume it anytime
  • plaintiff is named plaintiff in class action & claims of unnamed plaintiffs are still viable

Article III of the Constitution grants federal courts the power to decide actual cases and controversies—ie, disputes that are capable of judicial resolution. If further legal proceedings would no longer have an effect—often because the plaintiff's harm has been resolved—then an actual case or controversy typically ceases to exist. When this occurs, the plaintiff's claim is typically rendered moot and the case must then be dismissed.

However, one exception to this rule applies when the plaintiff whose claim has become moot is the named plaintiff in a certified class action (as seen here). If the claims of the unnamed plaintiffs in the class are still viable, then the class action will not be dismissed as moot. That is because, while the named plaintiff's personal claim has become moot, an actual case or controversy still exists for the unnamed plaintiffs' claims.

Here, the prisoner filed a class action in federal court, thereby serving as the named plaintiff. The prisoner's personal claim—that the commission's parole guidelines violate federal law—became moot when he was released from prison. However, an actual case or controversy still exists for the unnamed plaintiffs who have not been released (Choice A). Therefore, the court should deny the commission's motion to dismiss.

(Choice B) For a suit to be ripe for decision, the plaintiff must have experienced a real injury or immediate threat thereof. Here, the prisoner suffered actual harm when the commission denied the prisoner's request for parole, so this suit is ripe for decision.

(Choice C) The Eleventh Amendment prohibits foreign governments and private parties from suing a state in federal court. It does not prohibit private parties from suing the federal government in federal court (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A federal court typically must dismiss a case when the plaintiff's claim becomes moot. However, one exception applies when (1) a plaintiff whose claim is moot is the named plaintiff in a certified class action and (2) the claims of the unnamed plaintiffs in that class action are still viable.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case-or-controversy requirement).
  • U.S. Parole Comm'n v. Geraghty, 445 U.S. 388, 404 (1980) (holding that federal courts must not dismiss a class action when the named plaintiff's claim becomes moot so long as the claims of the unnamed plaintiffs are viable).
  • 32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 575 (2020) (defining mootness and its exceptions).

zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为该囚犯的诉讼尚未成熟，不宜裁决。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为 Eleventh Amendment 禁止在联邦法院提起此类诉讼。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Mootness & Class Actions

本题考察的是美国宪法第三条（Article III）中关于“案件或争议” (Case or Controversy) 的要求，特别是无意义原则 (Mootness) 在集体诉讼 (Class Action) 中的例外情况。

核心考点：无意义原则 (Mootness) 一般规则：如果原告的伤害已经消除（例如囚犯被释放），案件通常会因为“无意义” (Moot) 而被驳回，因为法院不再解决假设性的问题。

关键例外：集体诉讼 (Class Action)
如果集体诉讼在具名原告 (Named Plaintiff) 的诉求变为无意义之前已经获得法院的认证 (Certified)，那么该集体诉讼不会被驳回。

📅 案件时间线分析

1. 提起诉讼
囚犯挑战假释准则。
2. 集体诉讼认证 (Certification)
关键节点！法院认证了该集体。此时，未具名的集体成员 (Unnamed class members) 获得了独立的法律地位。
3. 囚犯获释
具名原告的个人诉求变为 Moot。
4. 动议驳回
法院应拒绝驳回，因为集体成员的诉求仍然存在 (Live controversy)。

⚖️ 选项深度解析

正确答案 A 不应批准，因为存在实际案件或争议。
虽然具名原告已出狱，但由于集体诉讼已被认证，未具名原告（其他仍在狱中的囚犯）的权益仍然受到威胁。因此，根据 Sosna v. Iowa 和 U.S. Parole Comm'n v. Geraghty 等判例，宪法第三条要求的“实际争议”依然存在。
错误选项 B 成熟性 (Ripeness)
成熟性关注的是“是否为时过早”。本案中，囚犯已经被拒绝假释，伤害已经发生，因此案件早已成熟。此选项混淆了概念。
错误选项 C 第十一修正案 (11th Amendment)
第十一修正案禁止私人起诉州政府 (State)。本案被告是联邦假释委员会 (Federal Parole Commission)，第十一修正案不适用。
错误选项 D 无意义 (Mootness)
这是最强的干扰项。如果这不是集体诉讼，或者在集体认证之前原告就出狱了，那么选项D就是对的。但因为集体已被认证，案件并未 Moot。
💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip):
在处理 Mootness 问题时，一旦看到 "Class Action" (集体诉讼)，立即检查时间点：
  • 如果 Certification (认证) 发生在原告诉求消失 之前 → 案件继续 (Not Moot)。
  • 如果原告在认证 之前 诉求消失 → 案件通常会被驳回 (Moot)，除非有其他例外（如“可重复但规避审查”）。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The National AIDS Prevention and Control Act is a new, comprehensive federal statute that was enacted to deal with the public health crisis caused by the AIDS virus. Congress and the President were concerned that inconsistent lower court rulings with respect to the constitutionality, interpretation, and application of the statute might adversely affect or delay its enforcement and thereby jeopardize the public health. As a result, they included a provision in the statute providing that all legal challenges concerning those matters may be initiated only by filing suit directly in the United States Supreme Court.
Is the provision authorizing direct review of the constitutionality, interpretation, or application of this statute only in the United States Supreme Court constitutional?

choices.A: No, because it denies persons who wish to challenge this statute the equal protection of the laws by requiring them to file suit in a court different from that in which persons who wish to challenge other statutes may file suit.
choices.B: No, because it is inconsistent with the specification in Article III of the original jurisdiction of the United States Supreme Court.
choices.C: Yes, because Article III provides that the jurisdiction of the United States Supreme Court is subject to such exceptions and such regulations as Congress shall make.
choices.D: Yes, because it is authorized by the Article I power of Congress to enact all laws that are "necessary and proper" to implement the general welfare.

questions.explanation:
SCOTUS jurisdiction
Type Definition Applicability
Original
(Congress cannot adjust) 		Case filed directly in SCOTUS Cases involving either:
  • • ambassador/public minister/consul or
  • • state as party
Appellate
(Congress may limit) 		Case filed after decision by either:
  • • lower federal court or
  • • highest state court
 All other cases by either:
  • • writ of certiorari or
  • • direct appeal (rare)
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States.

Article III gives the U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) original jurisdiction—ie, the authority to directly review a case—in two rare circumstances:

  • when a case affects an ambassador, public minister, or consul and
  • when a state is a party to the suit.

Congress cannot expand or restrict SCOTUS's original jurisdiction beyond Article III's specifications (Choice C). Since the statutory provision attempts to do so by authorizing SCOTUS to directly review challenges to the National AIDS Prevention and Control Act, it is unconstitutional.

(Choice A) This provision implicates the equal protection component of the Fifth Amendment because it treats persons challenging this statute differently than persons challenging other statutes. But since the provision does not substantially impact a fundamental right or protected class, it likely does not violate this component.

(Choice D) Article I allows Congress to enact laws that are "necessary and proper" (ie, reasonably appropriate) to carry out its enumerated powers—including the power to spend for the public's general welfare. But when doing so, it cannot violate other constitutional provisions (eg, Article III—as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Article III gives the U.S. Supreme Court original jurisdiction over cases (1) that affect an ambassador, public minister, or consul or (2) in which a state is a party. And Congress cannot alter SCOTUS's original jurisdiction.

📚 References
  • Marbury v. Madison, 5 U.S. 137, 174–76 (1803) (holding that Congress cannot alter the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction).
  • 32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 453 (2019) (defining original and appellate jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question: 该条款授权仅由 United States Supreme Court 对此法规的合宪性、解释或适用进行直接审查，此条款是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为它要求希望挑战该法规的人在一个不同于他人挑战其他法规时可以起诉的法院提起诉讼，这剥夺了他们受法律平等保护的权利。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为它与 Article III 中关于 United States Supreme Court 初始管辖权的规定不一致。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为 Article III 规定，United States Supreme Court 的管辖权受国会有权制定的例外和规章的约束。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为它得到了国会 Article I 权力的授权，即为实现普遍福祉而制定所有“必要和适当的”法律。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析
Article III Jurisdiction

正确答案：B 该条款违宪，因为它违反了宪法第三条（Article III）关于美国最高法院（SCOTUS）初始管辖权的规定。
核心法律规则

本题考察的是美国宪法中最基础的权力分立原则之一：国会是否有权改变最高法院的管辖权？

SCOTUS 的两类管辖权

根据 Article III, Section 2，最高法院的管辖权分为两类：

  • 初始管辖权 (Original Jurisdiction)：
    案件直接在最高法院起诉，不经过下级法院。
    范围极窄（宪法限定）：
    1. 涉及大使、公使、领事的案件；
    2. 州作为一方当事人的案件。
  • 上诉管辖权 (Appellate Jurisdiction)：
    审查下级法院的判决。
    范围：所有其他案件。
判例逻辑解析

著名的 Marbury v. Madison (1803) 确立了一个关键原则：

虽然国会可以通过“例外和规章条款” (Exceptions and Regulations Clause) 限制最高法院的上诉管辖权，但国会不能扩大或缩小宪法明确赋予最高法院的初始管辖权。

本题分析：

  • 题目中的法规允许公民直接向最高法院起诉（即行使初始管辖权）。
  • 该案件不涉及大使，也不是州与州之间的诉讼。
  • 因此，国会试图通过立法将本属于“上诉管辖”的案件变为“初始管辖”，这违背了 Article III 的明文规定。
⚠️ 常见陷阱 (Distractor C)
选项 C 引用了 "Exceptions and Regulations Clause"，这是 MBE 中极具迷惑性的选项。

记住：国会只能对上诉管辖权 (Appellate Jurisdiction) 制定例外或规章，而无权触碰初始管辖权 (Original Jurisdiction)。
其他选项为何错误
  • 选项 A (Equal Protection)： 虽然涉及程序差异，但通常只要有“合理依据” (Rational Basis) 即可通过审查。相比于选项 B 的结构性违宪（违反三权分立），这不是最致命的缺陷。
  • 选项 D (Necessary and Proper)： “必要和适当条款”赋予国会执行权力的手段，但这些手段不能违反宪法的其他明确禁令（如 Article III 对管辖权的限制）。
MBE 策略：区分 Original vs. Appellate Jurisdiction 是宪法题的高频考点。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state law provides for an award of damages against anyone who publishes the name of a rape victim. Pursuant to that law, a woman sued a local newspaper in state court after the newspaper identified her as a rape victim.
The state trial and appellate courts rejected the claim, holding that the state law was invalid under both the state constitution and the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution. The state supreme court affirmed, holding specifically: "We think that this well-intentioned law very likely violates the First Amendment of the federal Constitution. We need not, however, decide that issue, because the law assuredly violates our state constitution, which provides even greater protection to the right of the press to report the news."
The woman petitioned for review in the U.S. Supreme Court.
Is the U.S. Supreme Court likely to review the state supreme court judgment?

choices.A: No, because the First Amendment prohibits the imposition of liability for the publication of truthful information.
choices.B: No, because the judgment of the state supreme court rests upon an adequate and independent state-law ground.
choices.C: Yes, because the supremacy clause does not permit a state to create rights greater than those conferred by the federal Constitution.
choices.D: Yes, because the U.S. Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction extends to cases arising under federal law.

questions.explanation:
Adequate & independent state ground
(precludes SCOTUS review)
Adequate State ground fully resolves matter & application of federal law would not affect outcome
Independent State court did not rely on federal law to reach conclusion
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States

The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) may exercise its appellate jurisdiction to review a judgment of the highest court of a state if that judgment turned on federal law. But SCOTUS may not review a state court judgment that rests on an adequate and independent state ground—ie:

  • a state ground that fully resolves the matter such that the application of federal law would not affect the outcome of the case (adequate) and
  • the state court did not rely on federal law to reach its conclusion (independent).

Here, the state supreme court indicated that the state law very likely violates the U.S. Constitution. But the court also stated that it need not decide that federal issue because the law assuredly violates the state constitution. Since the state ground fully resolves the matter and the court did not rely on federal law to interpret the state constitution, SCOTUS is unlikely to review the state court judgment (Choice D).

(Choice A) The First Amendment freedom of the press generally bars liability for publicizing truthful information. But this does not provide a basis for SCOTUS to decline to review a case. Instead, review is improper here because the state court decision was based on an adequate and independent state ground.

(Choice C) The Article VI supremacy clause establishes that the U.S. Constitution and federal laws trump conflicting state laws. Therefore, states cannot restrict rights conferred by the U.S. Constitution. However, states are always free to create greater rights and protections than the U.S. Constitution does.

📌 Educational Objective

The U.S. Supreme Court cannot review a state court judgment that rests on an adequate and independent state ground—ie, (1) a state ground fully resolves the matter such that the application of federal law would not affect the outcome of the case and (2) the state court did not rely on federal law to reach its conclusion.

📚 References
  • Michigan v. Long, 463 U.S. 1032, 1041 (1983) (holding that a state supreme court can plainly state that its decision rests on adequate and independent state-law grounds).
  • 4 Am. Jur. 2d Appellate Review § 42 (2019) (explaining the adequate and independent state ground doctrine).
questions.zh-question:
一部州法律规定，对任何公布强奸案受害人姓名的人判处损害赔偿金。依据该法律，一名女性在当地一家报社指认其为强奸案受害人后，在州法院对该报社提起诉讼。

州初审法院和上诉法院驳回了该主张，认为该州法律根据州宪法和美国宪法第一修正案均属无效。州最高法院维持原判，并明确指出：“我们认为，这部用心良善的法律很可能违反了联邦宪法的第一修正案。然而，我们无需就此问题作出裁决，因为该法律确凿无疑地违反了我们的州宪法，而州宪法为新闻界报道新闻的权利提供了更强的保护。”

该女性请求美国最高法院进行复审。

美国最高法院是否可能复审州最高法院的判决？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为第一修正案禁止对发布真实信息的行为施加责任。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为州最高法院的判决依据的是充分且独立的州法律基础。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为至上条款不允许州创设比联邦宪法授予的权利更广泛的权利。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为美国最高法院的上诉管辖权延及根据联邦法律产生的案件。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law
核心考点：充分且独立的州法依据 Adequate and Independent State Grounds (AISG)

这是美国联邦最高法院（SCOTUS）管辖权的一个重要限制原则。如果州最高法院的判决完全基于州法律，且该依据足以支撑判决结果，SCOTUS 将拒绝复审。

规则详解 (The Rule)

SCOTUS 不会复审州法院的判决，如果该判决满足以下两个条件：

充分性
(Adequate)		 州法依据本身足以支持判决结果，无论联邦法律如何解释，结果都不会改变。
独立性
(Independent)		 州法院在解释州法时，没有依赖联邦法律或联邦判例。

背后的逻辑： 禁止咨询性意见 (Advisory Opinions)。如果 SCOTUS 即使推翻了州法院对联邦法的解释，案件结果（基于州法）依然不变，那么 SCOTUS 的判决就毫无实际意义，变成了仅仅是“建议”。

本题案情分析

在本题中，州最高法院做出了一个非常明确的声明（Plain Statement）：

"We need not... decide that [federal] issue, because the law assuredly violates our state constitution..."
（我们无需裁决联邦问题，因为该法律确凿无疑地违反了我们的州宪法……）

这意味着：即使 SCOTUS 介入并说“这不违反美国宪法第一修正案”，该州法律依然无效，因为它是基于州宪法被废止的。因此，SCOTUS 的介入不会改变结果。

选项解析
正确答案 B

不会复审，因为州最高法院的判决依据的是充分且独立的州法律基础。

这正是 AISG 原则的直接应用。州法院明确表示其判决独立于联邦宪法（Independent），且州宪法足以废除该法律（Adequate）。

选项 A 错误

虽然第一修正案确实保护真实信息的发布，但这涉及的是实体法问题 (Merits)，而不是管辖权问题 (Jurisdiction)。SCOTUS 首先必须确定是否有权复审，而在 AISG 存在的情况下，它无权复审。

选项 C 错误

这是一个常见的陷阱。至上条款 (Supremacy Clause) 禁止州法律剥夺联邦宪法赋予的权利（即不能低于联邦的“底线”）。但是，州完全有权通过州宪法赋予公民比联邦宪法更多的权利（即“天花板”可以更高）。

选项 D 错误

虽然 SCOTUS 对涉及联邦法律的问题拥有上诉管辖权，但 AISG 是一个例外。如果联邦问题的解决不能改变案件结果，SCOTUS 就不会行使管辖权。

💡 MBE 考试技巧：

在做此类题目时，寻找州法院的“明确声明” (Plain Statement)。

如果题目中州法院说：“虽然联邦法律可能也禁止这样做，但我们的判决是基于州宪法的”，或者“我们依据州法判决，联邦案例仅作参考”，那么这就是 AISG，SCOTUS 不会复审。

反之，如果州法院说：“我们对州宪法的解释与联邦最高法院对联邦宪法的解释一致”，那么这就不是独立的，SCOTUS 可以复审。
